employer: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Thoracic Surgery
descriptionHtml: The thoracic surgery service attracts national referrals for specialist complex surgery in both adults and children. Between the Royal Brompton, Harefield and Evelina sites we offer a wide range of thoracic treatments and perform in excess of 2,000 cases each year. We are the designated centre for sarcoma in London and the South East, seeing a range of metastatic, primary and chest wall disease. We have a strong record for performing VATS, and particularly, single port VATS lung resections. Since the arrival of a Da Vinci Xi robot on the Brompton site in 2025, followed by a Da Vinci 5 on the Harefield site in 2026, we have rapidly developed a busy RATS programme. We perform a large number of interventional bronchoscopies, with both rigid and fibre-optic techniques.  The Thoracic Surgery Department is currently expanding in response to the forecasted activity increase following the introduction of Targeted Lung Health Checks (TLHC). TLHC pilot schemes are already underway offering low-dose CT scans to those assessed as high risk. It is expected that we will see stage migration with more patients diagnosed with stage 1 lung cancer in our lung MDMs, this will contribute to the national ambition for 75% of cancers to be diagnosed at Stage 1 and 2 by 2028. As a result of the programme, there will be a higher proportion of patients who are suitable for curative treatment, in particular a higher number of thoracic surgery cases. Provide High Quality Care to Patients o The post-holder must be medically qualified and maintain GMC specialist registration, hold a licence to practice and fulfill the requirements for revalidation. o To develop and maintain the competencies required to carry out the duties required of the post. o To ensure patients are involved in decisions about their care and to respond to their views.  Leadership and Team Working o To demonstrate excellent leadership skills with regard to individual performance, clinical teams, the Trust and when participating in national or local initiatives. o To work collaboratively with all members of the multi-disciplinary team and Kings Health Partners as required.  Performance Management o To work with medical, nursing and managerial colleagues to ensure high performance in the following areas: o Clinical efficiency e.g. LOS reductions, reducing cancelled operations and DNA rates. o Quality of outcomes e.g. infection control targets, reducing re-admission rates. o Financial management e.g. identification, implementation and achievement of cost improvement programmes and participating in efforts to ensure services are provided cost effectively. o Operational efficiency e.g. waiting list activity and meeting cancer treatment targets.Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust comprises five of the UK's best known hospitals - Guy's, St Thomas', Evelina London Children's Hospital, Royal Brompton and Harefield - as well as community services in Lambeth and Southwark, all with a long history of high quality care, clinical excellence, research and innovation.  We are among the UK's busiest, most successful foundation trusts. We provide specialist care for patients including heart and lung, cancer and renal services as well as a full range of local hospital and community services for people in Lambeth and Southwark.  Royal Brompton and Harefield hospitals joined Guy's and St Thomas' in February 2021 and is the largest specialist heart and lung centre in the UK and among the largest in Europe. We provide treatment for people with heart and lung disease, including rare and complex conditions, offering some of the most sophisticated treatment that is available anywhere in the world.  Our integrated approach to caring for patients from before birth, through childhood, adolescence and into adulthood and old age has been replicated around the world and has gained Royal Brompton and Harefield an international reputation as a leader in heart and lung diagnosis, treatment and research.  We strive to recruit and retain the best staff as the dedication and skills of our employees lie at the heart of our organisation and ensure that our services are of the highest quality, safe and focused on our patients.

employer: Torbay and South Devon NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Dermatologist
descriptionHtml:
Applicants are invited for a part time Consultant Dermatologist post. The post holder would be joining a forward looking, expanding dermatology team, who are looking at innovative ways to address the rising local demand across Torbay. The plan for future dermatology services across the ICO includes more joined up care and an expansion of community-based clinics for patients requiring specialist input without secondary care facilities.

We are looking for a committed, team player who is enthusiastic and proactive. Application from an established Consultant or trainee within 6 months of obtaining Certificate of completion of specialist training (CCST) is welcome. Applicants should hold full GMC registration.

Our broad and inclusive team comprises: 5 Consultants, 5 Speciality Doctors, 2 CESR trainee and 2 Specialist Registrars. In addition, the team consists of six highly skilled specialist nurses, phototherapy nurses, admin staff and dedicated Dermatology HCAs. The department benefits from a Dermatology department with all team located within the same vicinity, which sits on the edge of the main hospital site.

A pre - interview visit to the department is strongly encouraged.

Informal enquires are welcome to Dr Rosie Davis (Clinical Lead) - Consultant Dermatologist rosie.davis1@nhs.net.

Torbay and South Devon NHS Foundation Trust is looking to appoint a dynamic, innovative and forward thinking full-time (10 PA per week) Consultant Dermatologist.

The successful applicant will join existing Consultants, Dr Rosie Davis ( Clinical Lead), Dr. Hannah Cookson (Clinical Lead), Dr Clement Ng, Dr Subhanitthaya Makris and Dr Christopher Hockin. The wider team consists of, 5 part time specialty doctors, 2 CESR trainee, 2 Registrars , 8 specialist nurses, 3 skin cancer nurse specialists, dedicated HCAs and a GPVTS trainee shared with Rheumatology.

Torbay Hospital is a medium sized, progressive and innovative District General Hospital providing acute services to South Devon. We are situated about 2 miles from the centre of Torquay and the dermatology department is based here. The Trust invested in new purpose-built Dermatology facilities and offices in autumn 2017. The Dermatology team now have dedicated consultation / examination suites, 2 minor surgery rooms, phototherapy and team offices. This is located in a separate building at the edge of the hospital site. Additional minor surgery rooms have been retained in the main outpatients of the hospital, along with access to the paediatric outpatient facility.

Potential applicants are encouraged to contact the department and Dr Rosie Davis (Lead Clinician).

Why Work With Us

employer: Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and wear (CNTW) NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist STH Tyneside Psychosis/Non Psychosis Adult CTT
descriptionHtml:
At CNTW we strive to provide the BEST CARE, delivered by the BEST PEOPLE, to achieve the BEST OUTCOME. CNTW is on a mission to empower people to make the most of their lives through our outstanding, joined-up healthcare services.

As a Consultant, you will know what it means to achieve this by leading a team. Striving for a better service. Working with us you'll be part of a strong team, challenge yourself, build a career, and teach us what we don't know, and you'll be working towards our vision to be better every day through excellence, compassion and expertise in all we do And as a specialist in Adult community Psychiatry you will work with the CPNs and integrated team psychologists to provide medical expertise for CTT patients across psychosis and non-psychosis pathways. The Team is one of the Trust's pilot sites for the Community Transformation work. You will be an active member in supporting the Trust and your team during this process.

The job is a 8PAs a week over 4 days and you will be working alongside the multidisciplinary team, including resident doctors, and wider clinical teams, you will be the clinical expert from a medical perspective to ensure best practice care is delivered and support the team.

The post holder will offer medical input to the Step up hub team South Tyneside. The Step up Hub team Provides an enhanced intensity of interventions to patients with high complex needs , usually in stepped care or supported accommodation.

The post-holders will provide Consultant clinical leadership to the service and will assume consultant psychiatrist responsibility for their proportion of patients being looked after by the team. This includes assuming Responsible Clinician status for patients under their care, including patients subject to Community Treatment Orders, taking a lead on compliance with the Mental Health Act and CQC requirements. They will participate, directly and indirectly, in the assessment of patients referred to the service and in drawing up care plans which will address the patients' psychiatric, physical, and social needs. They will carry out detailed psychiatric assessments of patients as clinically indicated to allow accurate diagnoses and contribute to their treatment plans, including pharmacological management of psychotropic medication.

The post-holder will forge good working relationships with other psychiatrists across the Directorate in order to encourage appropriate referrals and assure a cooperative approach to the care of patients. They will be linked in with other Consultants and supported to join peer groups. They will also provide consultation and advice to members of the MDT and primary care colleagues.

Why us?

  • Up to 8k relocation package
  • 30 days study leave (every 3 years)
  • Flexible working opportunities created with you involved in your job plan
  • Remote working available as suits service needs
  • Dedicated and protected SPA time
  • Focus on creating a healthy workforce by investing heavily in health and wellbeing accessible support including emotional, physical, social, psychological financial and career well being
  • Teaching and research opportunities available
  • Stimulating CPD sessions and programs including mentoring, medical leadership, and coaching
  • Teaching opportunities in our brand-new state of the art Medical Education Centre
  • Employee Excellence awards
  • Plus, lots more employee benefits including discounts. Find out more at www.thriveatcntw.co.uk

As an added bonus, the Trust is located in the Northeast of England and Cumbria which is an area of outstanding natural beauty, containing national parks, ancient heritage sites and major cities supported by excellent national and international transport links. The area is predominantly rural and contains the Lake District National Park which is considered one of England's finest areas of natural beauty.

employer: Royal United Hospitals Bath NHS Foundation Trust
title: Acute Medicine Consultant
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for the post of Consultant in Acute Medicine at the Royal United Hospitals Bath NHS Foundation Trust. This is a great opportunity for an enthusiastic individual to join a dynamic team of consultants at a time when the service is expanding from investment.

We are happy to support applicants who wish to work full time, part time or in a flexible working pattern. We are interested to hear from you if you have a passion for Acute Medicine, but also want to maintain a specialist interest in another area, as most of our team work in this way. We are a warm and welcoming MDT, proud to work in this fast-paced environment using evidence-based best practice. We would like to hear from candidates who want to develop skills in this engaging specialism, or more experienced physicians who can consolidate their own skills whilst supporting others.

The Acute Medicine service sits within Medical Division, and as part of the Integrated Front Door Service. We provide a responsive interface between primary and secondary care needs, identifying and managing those unwell patients who require inpatient acute hospital treatment, while also supporting primary care clinicians in managing other patients safely and effectively in the community.

If you would like to know more about this opportunity, please contact our Clinical Lead, Dr Sarah Gillett on sarahgillett@nhs.net, for an informal chat.

We have a rolling rota which encompasses 7 day cover for the Medical Short Stay (MSS) unit and patients remaining in the Medical Assessment Unit (MAU) for daily ward rounds, and post take rounds.

Our Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC) area, located next to the Emergency Department and MAU is a purpose-built space for this key front door service. The consultants are supported by specialty doctors, Medical Nurse Practitioners and nurses, to assess and treat patients referred from primary care, that require urgent assessment and diagnostic tests but do not necessarily require admission. We also care for patients referred by our own ED and acute medical teams, enabling a safe and supported and timely discharge from hospital. The SDEC service manages a dedicated phone line, for community partners to access consultant advice and guidance, supporting patients to be given the right care in the right place.

MAU has a target length of stay of up to 12-24 hours and is for the initial assessment and management of acutely ill medical patients prior to discharge or admission into the hospital. The RUH benefits from a separate front door frailty service and a dedicated Older Persons Assessment Unit.

MSS is for patients who need a 1 or 2-night stay in hospital, and these patients remain under the care of the acute medicine team, receiving consultant led ward rounds and MDT care.

At the RUH we put people at the heart of what we do, working together as one team to make a difference for our patients, each other, and our community. No matter what your role is, we value everyone's contribution in supporting the exceptional, person-centred care we pride ourselves on.

We are proud to be in the top 20 best hospitals to work for in the country.

We are committed to creating a compassionate and inclusive environment. This can be seen in our growing community of staff networks - celebrating successes and creating opportunities to listen and learn. We value our differences, champion kindness and civility, and truly believe that diversity makes us stronger.

A culture of learning, developing and innovating is the thread that runs throughout our whole organisation. We want to support you to thrive, taking your career to its full potential.

We value staff well-being, with a well-established programme of support. We believe in a holistic approach spanning all aspects of living a healthy life, including physical, emotional, spiritual and financial well-being. We've even got a pool!

We are committed to supporting you and hope you want to join our team. In the meantime, find out more about living and working the beautiful historic city of Bath, learn about our extensive package of staff benefits, and read about how we're providing healthcare fit for the future with the landmark Dyson Cancer Centre and our passion for research.

employer: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locally Employed Doctor (Higher) in Burns and Plastics
descriptionHtml:
Note this post is currently fixed term until February 2027 due to gaps within the Deanery rota numbers. Depending on future allocations this post may extend further. An exciting opportunity for hard-working and ambitious plastic surgeons to join a well-established registrar program in one of the largest Burns, Plastics and Hands units in the country. This job is tailored according to the experience of the candidate and would be very suitable for candidates seeking a national training number (NTN) in Plastic Surgery. We have a robust track record in registrars working in this post securing a NTN. 100% of the Pre-ST3 Fellows appointed in August 2022 were offered NTNs in National Selection 2023. We take pride that our non-deanery trainees have the same training opportunities as deanery trainees. Note there may be opportunities from Feb - May 2027 pending later allocation information.

The post holder is expected to:

-Lead morning handover, trauma meeting and ward round

-Provide supervision to the core-level doctors

-Lead night handover when on call

-Undertake trauma lists under appropriate supervision when on call, including at weekends

-Assist consultants in clinic and theatre lists

-Responsibility for the safe and effective care of inpatients and outpatients under the care of the burns, plastics and hand surgery teams

-Liaise with members of the MDT, including plastics outreach nurses, hand therapists, rehabilitation therapists, psychologists, burns outreach nurses etc.

-Engage in teaching and training of the junior doctors

-The JSDs work a Full Shift Rota (with prospective cover for annual leave, study leave and bank holidays)

University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust strives to have an inclusive culture where everyone feels like they belong, can thrive, knows that they add value and feels valued. We do this by developing compassionate and culturally competent leaders, being values driven in all that we do and by creating a welcoming and inclusive workplace that thrives on the diversity of our people. As such we want to attract and recruit talented individuals from all backgrounds, and for each of you to feel supported for the diversity you bring, to achieve your full potential. For those staff with a disability, including physical disability, long term health condition, mental health or neurodiverse condition, this also means being committed to making reasonable adjustments needed for you to carry out your role.

title: Salaried GP and GP Partner Roles (6 to 8 Sessions)
descriptionHtml:
The Lighthouse Group Practice is seeking up to three GPs to join our friendly and supportive team. We welcome applications from both Salaried GPs and experienced GPs interested in Partnership opportunities. We are looking for GPs able to work 6 to 8 sessions per week and would welcome the opportunity to discuss how you could become part of our established and supportive practice team.This is an excellent opportunity to join a progressive practice that is investing in its future, including a new purpose-built medical centre at Bransbury Park, expected to open in 2027.

For GPs joining the Partnership, there will be the opportunity to play an active role in the strategic direction and future development of the practice. Supported by an experienced Business Partner and management team, Partners are encouraged to contribute to service innovation, business planning, workforce development, and decision-making, without the requirement for a property buy-in.

As a GP at our practice, you will become an integral member of our friendly and supportive multidisciplinary team, delivering high-quality, patient-centred care to our diverse practice population. Working alongside experienced GPs, nurse practitioners, nurses, pharmacists, and the wider primary care team, you will contribute to the continued development of our services and the delivery of excellent clinical care.

The Lighthouse Group Practice is a friendly, forward-thinking GP training practice providing care to approximately 12,000 patients across two sites: Southsea Medical Centre and Devonshire Avenue Surgery. We have been an established training practice since 2008 and are proud to support the development of the next generation of GPs.

As an active member of a progressive Primary Care Network serving around 44,000 patients, and with a well-established Integrated Neighbourhood Team (INT), we work collaboratively to deliver high-quality, patient-centred care.

Our future is equally exciting, with a new purpose-built medical centre at Bransbury Park due to open in late 2027, replacing our Devonshire Avenue site and providing modern facilities for patients and staff.

Based in the vibrant coastal city of Portsmouth, we offer an excellent work-life balance, with beaches, the South Downs National Park, and direct rail links to London all within easy reach.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are recruiting up to 6 sessions at NPC Spring Terrace, North Shields on a fixed term basis for 12 months. This is an excellent opportunity for a GP who is passionate about delivering high-quality patient care and is keen to play a key role in shaping the future of a thriving practice.

NPC Spring Terrace is a welcoming, community-focused practice serving the population of North Shields and surrounding areas, with a strong commitment to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care. As part of Northumbria Primary Care and the wider NPC North Tyneside neighbourhood, the practice benefits from a diverse multidisciplinary team and a collaborative network across four local sites, providing opportunities for shared learning, peer support, and service resilience.

As a teaching practice, Spring Terrace Health Centre takes great pride in developing our future work force in primary care. This includes GP registrars, medical students, nursing students and the continued development of all staff.

As a practice Spring Terrace has been on a journey of quality improvement over recent years and is subsequently growing its patient list, clinical space and workforce.

Please note we reserve the right to close this vacancy prior to the closing date once the required number of suitable applications have been received.

As a GP Practice which is part of Northumbria Primary Care, we work with flexibility and independence to run the surgery based on what is best for our patients and staff, and additionally we have the regular and consistent support of the management team to help us to focus on what is clinically important.

As a Salaried GP the post holder will be a key clinician within the team. A job plan will be agreed with you to provide general medical services and deal with a wide range of health needs in a primary care setting.

NPC is a pioneering partnership with local GPs and now manages several GP practices with around 120,000 registered patients in Northumberland and North Tyneside.

As an NPC GP we can offer some great benefits some of which are:

  • Protected time for QI and indirect clinical care.
  • 15 minute appointments.
  • Opportunities for portfolio working and development of specialist clinical interest roles.
  • Access to all benefits of Northumbria healthcare; lease cars; home electronics; health and wellbeing offers.
  • Support with education, monthly education timeout sessions as well as a quarterly, NPC practice wide education sessions covering a range of topics dictated by the needs of our clinicians. Free access to Red Whale, mentorship and coaching.
  • Support managing medication requests, reviews and document management (coders) to increase efficiency and reduce the admin burden on GPs.

Although part of a larger organisation, NPC, as a GP practice, we work with flexibility and independence to run the surgery based on what is best for our patients and staff, and additionally we have the regular and consistent support of the management team to help us to focus on what is clinically important.

We are a forward-thinking organisation and as part of our culture we are embracing new technologies to improve the services we offer our patients. We understand the importance of listening to our patients and are not afraid to make changes following feedback.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to welcome a motivated and enthusiastic salaried GP to join our friendly, patient focussed team. We can offer an attractive salary and would be pleased to provide more information and/or the option of an informal visit to meet our Practice team.

For further information about both the Practice and the post please contact our Practice Manager.

We have 6 sessions available on Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday each week.

We are looking for a professional who is committed to providing consistently high standards of patient focussed care and who will contribute to the wider clinical team and the development of the practice.

Key Responsibilities include :-

  • Assess, diagnose and manage patients across urgent, primary and community care settings.
  • Prescribe, investigate, refer and escalate care as clinically required.
  • Deliver face-to-face, telephone and remote consultations.
  • Maintain clear and accurate clinical records.
  • Provide high-quality patient communication and safety-netting.
  • Work effectively within multidisciplinary teams and established clinical pathways.
  • Support safe, patient-centred care while meeting governance and safeguarding requirements.
  • Contribute to service quality, patient safety and continuous improvement initiatives

This would be an ideal opportunity for either an experienced GP looking for a change or a newly qualified GP looking to make their mark. You will be joining a friendly, supportive team in a well-established, stable practice with good facilities and excellent opportunities for personal development.

We are a semi-rural dispensing practice of approximately 9,750 patients based in the historic market town of Evesham, on the edge of the Cotswolds, and with excellent transport links to Cheltenham, Stratford-upon-Avon, Birmingham, Oxford and London.

We pride ourselves on promoting a traditional caring ethos of General Practice, whilst evolving within a modern healthcare environment.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a salaried GP to join our team at Plas Meddyg Surgery in the historic market town of Ruthin. We welcome applications from both newly qualified and experienced GPs.

We are a well-run, single-site dispensing practice serving a growing population of just over 11,000 patients. As an established training practice, we support GP registrars, medical students, paramedics, nurses and nurse practitioners, with learning and mutual support embedded in our everyday work.

Essential criteria

  • Full GMC registration with a licence to practise.
  • Inclusion on the GMC GP Register and the NHS Wales Medical Performers List by the start date.
  • Commitment to safe, high-quality, patient-centred care.
  • Effective communication, teamwork and organisational skills.
  • Commitment to continuing professional development, clinical governance and quality improvement.

Desirable criteria

  • Experience of working in UK general practice.
  • Interest or experience in teaching, training or supervising healthcare professionals.
  • Interest in developing a clinical specialism or contributing to service development, including primary care research.
  • Experience of working in a dispensing practice.
  • Welsh language skills.

Why join us?

  • Shared responsibility: Partners and salaried colleagues work alongside one another, sharing clinical workload and on-call duties, with ready access to advice and support.
  • More time for clinical work: Our established workflows and experienced administrative team help clinicians focus on work that requires their expertise.
  • Supported home visiting: A dedicated cluster ANP home-visiting team undertakes most visits, working closely with us and involving GPs when patients need more complex assessment or care.
  • A practice open to change: We welcome ideas and continually improve how we work, using innovation to make care more effective and workloads more manageable.
  • Rewarding community medicine: We provide GP-led care to an engaged population, with opportunities to support self-care and build meaningful clinical relationships. Our partners also provide medical cover at Ruthin Community Hospital, with access to community inpatient care for suitable patients who do not require acute admission.

We are a busy practice with high demand, but we take pride in consistently delivering high standards of care through teamwork, efficient systems and shared clinical responsibility.

Start date: Ideally 1st April 2027, with flexibility for the right candidate

employer: Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Manchester - Central East CMHT
descriptionHtml:
Community Mental Health Teams (CMHTs) provide multi-disciplinary assessment, treatment and care of individuals with severe and enduring mental health problems. They provide a service to individuals from 16 years of age up to 70 years of age with a diagnosed functional mental health problem.

Clinical role

  • Undertake assessments of referrals/ admissions to the service
  • Diagnose and formulate management plans in complex presentations.
  • Provide management in treatment resistant and complex presentations
  • Assessment and management of risk including of vulnerability, suicide risk, risks to health and safety and risk of harm to others.
  • Preparation of Mental Health Review Tribunal and Managers' Hearings reports and attendance at subsequent hearings.
  • Work in a collaborative way with multidisciplinary teams including external partners.
  • Work in partnership with psychiatrists from partner providers such as Forensic and Rehabilitation Psychiatrists.

Leadership role

  • Lead clinical decision making in the multidisciplinary team to ensure the delivery of high quality care
  • Develop service clinical priorities in line with national and professional guidance and standards
  • Engage with service transformation programmes including attendance at Consultant meetings for their service and directorate.

Greater Manchester Mental Health (GMMH) Foundation Trust employs over6,400members of staff, who deliver services from more than160locations.

We provide inpatient and community-based mental health care for people living in Bolton, the city of Manchester, Salford,Trafford and the borough of Wigan, and a wide range of specialist mental health and substance misuse services across Greater Manchester, the north west of England and beyond.

Greater Manchester is one of the world's most innovative, original and exciting places to live and work. From the beauty of the surrounding countryside to the heart of the vibrant inner city with great shopping, entertainment and dining options.

Wherever you go you will experience a great northern welcome with people famed for their warmth, humour and generosity.

Our people enjoy their work, have opportunities to learn and develop their skills and are encouraged to generate new ideas that improve care for our service users.

title: TPD for Clinical Radiology North Central London (Barts)
descriptionHtml:
An outstanding individual is sought to fulfil the role of Training Programme Director for Clinical Radiology for North Central and East London (Barts scheme).

The role of Training Programme Director is to work with and support the Postgraduate Dean in leading the delivery of a wide range of functions within their specialty, aligned to the NHS England mandate. The Programme Director will ensure that both national standards, determined by the Royal College and also guidelines and standards established within Clinical Radiology are met.

The successful applicants will work closely with the Head of School, other Clinical Radiology TPDs, School team including; PGMDE Business Manager, Postgraduate Dean, and other key departments including Quality.

They will work with the Postgraduate Dean to produce doctors who will strive for the highest standards of patient-centred care and commit themselves to a lifetime of professional development.

Working collaboratively to ensure our healthcare workforce has the right knowledge, skills, values, and behaviours to deliver accessible, compassionate care.

The Programme Director will ensure that both national standards, determined by the Royal College, and guidelines and standards established within Clinical Radiology are met. Responsibilities will include:

  • To oversee the Specialty's Regional Training Programme
  • Specialty-specific matters and trainee/trainer concerns
  • Recruitment to training posts and programmes
  • Postgraduate programme management, including assessments, progression, rotations, support and remediation, OOP management, trainee management careers support, less than full-time training, inter-deanery transfer, academic training and other related work-streams.

The ideal candidate will be an experienced NHS Consultant with a thorough understanding of Clinical Radiology training across the region and who will also have strong leadership and communication skills and be able to work effectively as a member of a multi-professional team.

NHS England has a wide range of statutory functions, responsibilities and regulatory powers. These are focused on supporting the wider NHS to deliver high quality care, as well as doing those things that are best done once for the whole NHS.

Our staff bring expertise across clinical, operational, commissioning, technology, data science, cyber security, software engineering, education, and commercial specialisms -- enabling us to design and deliver high-quality NHS services.

In March 2025, the Government announced that NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care will increasingly merge functions, ultimately leading to NHS England being fully integrated into the department.

If you currently work within the NHS and if successful at interview, we will initiate an Inter Authority Transfer (IAT) via the Electronic Staff Record (ESR).This retrieves key data from your current or previous NHS employer to support onboarding, including competency status, Continuous Service Dates (CSD), and annual leave entitlement. You may opt out at any stage of the process.

Colleagues with a contractual office base are expected to spend, on average, at least 40% of their time working in our offices.

We cannot offer visa sponsorship for any vacancies.

employer: St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant in Acute Medicine +/- complimentary specialty
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic physician to join our team of 16 Acute Physicians as a Locum Consultant to participate in the on-going development and evolution of our Acute Medicine Unit (AMU) and to play a key role in the management of emergency ambulatory and in-patient medical admissions.

This post has been developed in order to be able to deliver a sustainable model of acute care. The London Quality Standards recognise the importance of a dedicated Acute Physician team leading acute care. This post present an excellent opportunity for a clinician, with experience and considerable understanding of all aspects of acute medicine with or without a specialist interest, to join a team dynamic team of physicians committed to the delivery of the highest standard of patient care. This individual will be expected to contribute to the ongoing development of the clinical interface with both Primary Care and the Emergency Department at St George's.

Scope of the Department:

The Acute Medicine Unit (AMU) at St George's Hospital was established in 2000. Since then the unit has undergone several reconfigurations in order to modernise our ambulatory unit. The AMU comprises:

The 51 bedded AMU, which includes a 15 bedded Acute Dependency Unit (ADU) with 5 dedicated Level 2 beds, which benefits from daily Consultant led ward rounds and intensive care consultant involvement.

The Medical SDEC Unit also known as the Ambulatory Assessment Area (AAA) consists of 10 chairs, 6 trolleys and 4 clinic rooms. One of the trollies in a side room. We benefit from a dedicated ultrasound service on a daily basis within the unit and also rapid access (same day/next day) CT scanning slots. The unit is supported by a team of experienced advanced nurse practitioners/nurse practitioners, nurses and co-ordinator. The AAA team are working to develop further our Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC) pathways.

Amyand is a 28 bedded short stay ward for patients with a predicted length of stay of less than 5 days, which is run as part of the Acute Medicine Unit.

The Acute Medicine Care Group has continually evolved in recent years in order to meet the demand for acute care. This has increased consultant input within the initial 24-48 hours following admission. This post is pivotal to the assessment and management of acutely unwell adult patients. We are also striving to continually improve geriatric and frailty services which most recently has seen integration across the acute and community based teams

The current job plan has been designed to provide a sustainable post in Acute Medicine with or without a complementary specialty. The job plan is designed on an annualised basis which allows some flexibility. There will be an expected commitment to all aspects of the service including; the acute medicine on call rota, physician of the week and Amyand ward rotas, weekend working and the medical SDEC (Same Day Emergency Care).

The appointee is expected to participate in undergraduate, postgraduate and multi-disciplinary education programmes and to play a full part in Clinical Governance.

employer: Barking, Havering and Redbridge University Hospitals NHS Trust
title: Locum Consultant Neurosurgeon - Neurooncology and Functional
descriptionHtml:
BHRUT is seeking an experienced Locum Consultant Neurosurgeon with an interest in Neuro-Oncology and Functional Neurosurgery to join its Regional Neurosciences service.

BHRUT provides specialist neurosurgical care across Essex and Outer North East London, including neuro-oncology, functional neurosurgery, neurovascular, skull base, pituitary and complex spinal services, supported by dedicated theatres, a neurosurgical ward and Neuro ICU.

The successful candidate will provide consultant-level care in neuro-oncology and functional neurosurgery, including complex brain tumour surgery, MDT participation, outpatient clinics and elective operating.

The post holder will also support the wider neurosurgical service, including general cranial neurosurgery and consultant on-call duties, in line with the agreed job plan.

The post holder will provide consultant-led neurosurgical care within a regional neurosciences service, delivering high-quality, evidence-based and patient-centred care across elective, urgent and emergency pathways.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Provide consultant assessment, diagnosis, surgical treatment and follow-up for patients with brain and central nervous system tumours.
  • Undertake specialist neuro-oncology outpatient clinics, inpatient care, elective operating lists and multidisciplinary team participation.
  • Apply contemporary neuro-oncology and functional neurosurgical techniques to maximise safe tumour resection while preserving neurological, cognitive and quality-of-life outcomes.
  • Participate actively in the regional neuro-oncology MDT, working collaboratively with oncology, neurology, neuroradiology, neuropathology, neuropsychology, rehabilitation, palliative care and specialist nursing colleagues.
  • Provide clear, compassionate and evidence-based communication with patients and their families, including discussion of complex treatment options, risks, prognosis and expected functional outcomes.
  • Participate fully in the consultant neurosurgical on-call rota, providing emergency neurosurgical assessment and management, remote advice and imaging review for referring hospitals, and appropriate cross-cover for consultant colleagues

We're an organisation that is getting better and better and our improvements are driven by a determination to deliver care we're proud of and our patients are happy with.

They are benefitting from a new electronic patient record (we were the last acute trust in London to introduce one) and our maternity services have been rated good by the Care Quality Commission.

We operate from two main sites - KGH in Goodmayes and Queen's Hospital in Romford. We have two busy emergency departments with more than 346,000 people visiting them last year. We're campaigning to secure the £35m we need to transform the A&E at Queen's and get rid of corridor care.

We're proud of our regional Neurosciences Centre, Radiotherapy Centre and Hyper Acute Stroke Unit. We're also part of the North East London Cancer Alliance.

We run a Women's Health Hub in Ilford; an Ageing Well Centre in Hornchurch; and Community Diagnostic Centres (CDC) at Barking Community Hospital and at St George's Health and Wellbeing Hub. These CDCs are open 12 hours a day, 7 days a week.

The majority of our 8,400 staff - who come from 146 different countries - live in the three diverse London boroughs we serve and are from black, Asian and minority ethnic groups. Many can work flexibly and more than 400 of them are on our Ofsted accredited apprenticeship programmes. We're proud to be a London Living Wage employer.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Higham Ferrers Surgery is seeking an enthusiastic and compassionate GP to join our friendly, supportive team. This is an excellent opportunity for a clinician who values continuity of care and enjoys working in a smaller practice where strong relationships with patients and colleagues are at the heart of what we do. The successful candidate will provide high-quality clinical care, contribute to the ongoing development of the practice, and play an active role in shaping our future direction. An interest in teaching and mentoring would be highly valued, with opportunities to support and supervise our resident doctors.We welcome applications from GPs, with working hours and sessions negotiable, and an immediate start available.

What We Offer

title: Trust Doctor in Obstetrics & Gynaecology (ST5-7 level)
descriptionHtml:
Barts Health NHS Trust

Trust Doctor in Obstetrics & Gynaecology (ST5-7 level)

With special interest in Maternal-Fetal Medicine

Whipps Cross University Hospital

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an enthusiastic doctor to join the current Obstetrics and Gynaecology team as a Trust Doctor at Barts Health NHS Trust for 1 year.

Barts Health NHS Trust was created on 1 April 2012 and is the largest in the UK.

The post will be based at The Whipps Cross University Hospital . This is a non-training post but will provide valuable experience in maternal-fetal medicine and high risk obstetrics for those wishing to secure future posts, including at consultant level for applicants who already hold CCT.

Individuals will require full GMC Registration and should be post MRCOG. These posts are aimed at UK or Overseas trainee obstetricians at ST 5+ level or above, and for EU trained individuals with the appropriate level of clinical experience. The successful applicant should have already achieved basic obstetric ultrasound skills. There will be an out of hours component to the job as a senior registrar with responsibility for supervising a more junior SpR on delivery suite and covering gynaecology emergencies.

Opportunities will be given to work with the fetal medicine team together with attending the range of maternal medicine clinics offered at Whipps Cross. Post holders will be trained in obstetric ultrasound and the management of maternal medical conditions as well as in high risk antenatal and intrapartum obstetrics. There will also be opportunities to develop obstetric leadership skills and obstetric ATSM's may be supported depending on the candidates interests. Successful candidates will be encouraged to participate in teaching, research, audit and journal club. In line with our commitment to improving the working lives of our junior doctors, the duties and hours are fully compliant with the New Deal initiative

Barts Health is one of the largest NHS trusts in the country, and one of Britain's leading healthcare providers.

Our vision is to be a high-performing group of NHS hospitals, renowned for excellence and innovation, and providing safe and compassionate care to our patients in east London and beyond. That means being a provider of excellent patient safety, known for delivering consistently high standards of harm-free care and always caring for patients in the right place at the right time. It also means being an outstanding place to work, in which our WeCare values and behaviours are visible to all and guide us in how we work together.

We strive to live by our WeCare values and are committed to promoting inclusion, where every staff member has a sense of belonging. We value our differences and fully advocate, cultivate and support an inclusive working environment.

employer: Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Trust
title: Consultant Clinical Neurophysiologist
descriptionHtml:
Substantive full time Consultant Clinical Neurophysiology opportunity at RNOH

The Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Trust (RNOH) is seeking to appoint a Consultant Clinical Neurophysiologist to join our specialist clinical team. The service has undergone a review to ensure a continued and sustainable service for the future and we are delighted to offer a fulltime opportunity at this prestigious hospital.

This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to a dynamic and forward-thinking neurophysiology service at one of the UK's and the world`s leading specialist orthopaedic hospitals.

This is a fulltime position (10 PAs) which offers some flexibility in the working schedule, as EEG reporting, can often be done remotely.

The role also includes the opportunity to engage with both NHS and Private Care Unit (PCU) services. The postholder will contribute to delivering safe, high-quality services for all patient groups, ensuring consistency of practice, adherence to Trust policies, and effective collaboration with multidisciplinary teams across both service streams.

We would strongly advise any interested applicants in contacting the service leads to discuss any details or clarifications required for this post. We welcome applicants internally and externally to the UK. The team has a great track record of multidisciplinary working, team working and in providing excellent support to new colleagues.

The successful applicant will provide a full range of nerve conduction studies (NCS) and electromyography (EMG) services, a significant proportion of which are complex referrals from the Peripheral Nerve Injury (PNI) unit. The appointed person would be expected to be able to undertake this on all available equipment, currently Cadwell Sierra summit EMG/EP systems.

They will also be required to support physiologist led carpal tunnel clinics & report on these tests. The successful applicant will be required to report on EEGs. The department performs a substantial amount of intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM) during spinal & peripheral nerve explorative surgery.

This part of the service is physiologist led but governed by the consultant neurophysiologist. Whilst 'hands on' involvement is not expected it could provide an interesting adjunct to the job role.

The Job description is indicative, pending College approval.

  • Rated Good ,by the CQC
  • Two sites, one in central London and one in Stanmore - which has recently opened The Stanmore Building, a new, state-of-the-art inpatient facility
  • Our Research and Innovation Centre works closely with our main academic partner, University College London
  • Recognised as a centre of excellence, leading on national initiatives, such as theGetting It Right First Time (GIRFT)Programme
  • Further major redevelopment underway across the Stanmore site - improving and modernising our facilities to maintain our position as the UK's leading centre for orthopaedic medicine
  • In the NHS staff survey, over 90% of our staff were satisfied with the quality of care they are able to give to patients - the best result of any NHS Trust in the country
  • Our staff also indicated that they had the best experience of appraisals as compared to all other NHS Trusts.

This is a great time to join us and play a critical role in the next stage of RNOH's journey to achieving an outstanding CQC rating.

We are committed to equal opportunities in employment and offer a range of flexible working practices. Part-time and job share applications will be considered.

We reserve the right to close this advert early due to the volume of applicants. Please apply as soon as possible to avoid disappointment.

employer: Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board
title: Consultant Intensivist & Emergency Medicine
descriptionHtml:
Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board is one of the largest Health Boards in Wales and was formed in 2019. It is situated near of the vibrant cities of Cardiff, Swansea and Bristol and is enriched with magnificent scenery including beautiful beaches and the stunning Brecon Beacons national park. We take our staff wellbeing seriously and have dedicated wellbeing rooms and mindfulness sessions. All our staff are issued with a staff discount card providing multiple savings in shops and restaurants. You don't have to speak Welsh to work in our organisation but we will give you the opportunity to learn.

We take staff development seriously and encourage everyone to flourish and progress during their time with us.

For those of you with a young family childcare is available on all three acute hospital sites. There are excellent schools and affordable housing both within and just outside the Health Board.

Whether its paddle boarding, caving, outdoor swimming or singing in a male voice choir- Cwm Taf Morgannwg will provide a fantastic work-life balance for everyone.

oSPA allocation as per Welsh Contract. Negotiated on appointment, evidenced and reviewed annually at job plan. Core SPA 1.5 as minimum oAll new Consultants will be "buddied" with existing consultant for support/mentoring oSPA time for new Consultants for initial development oOut-of-hours clinical support from Consultant(s) on other two sites oFree access to "UpToDate" oHealth Board laptop with Microsoft 365 and home working capabilities oRemote access to Philips ICCA Intensive Care Electronic Patient Record and Welsh Clinical Portal. oNamed Consultant to support doctors who are new to working in the UK oShared office space and hot-desking capabilities on all three sites oFree car parking on all sites, access to NHS Wales Salary Sacrifice scheme for fleet cars oDaily Sit-Rep meetings to facilitate mutual aid across the Health Board oMonthly, site specific meeting with Clinical Director and Directorate Manager oBi-monthly pan-CTM meetings with entire Critical Care team

Cwm Taf Morgannwg (CTM) University Health Board, part of NHS Wales, serves a large population across a diverse and beautiful region, steeped in history and heritage. With nearly 13,500 staff, our health board is one of Wales's largest employers.

Together, we are Team CTM; a workforce dedicated to offering excellent patient care and support to the 450,000 people across our three regions, Bridgend, Merthyr Tydfil, and Rhondda Cynon Taf. We operate three District General hospitals, several community hospitals, primary and community care facilities.

CTM's location offers the best of South Wales, just 20 minutes from Cardiff's vibrant city life, the natural beauty of the Brecon Beacons, and the serene coastline at Ogmore. Whether you enjoy lively urban amenities, peaceful countryside, or seaside escapes, our location makes an ideal setting for both work and personal life.

Our CTM 2030 Strategy--Our Health, Our Future--focuses on uniting our region around shared health and wellbeing goals. Our values guide us daily:

o We listen, learn, and improve

o We treat everyone with respect

o We work together as one team

CTM employees enjoy benefits including; a leading pension, generous leave, flexible work, career growth, and access to ongoing learning and development.

At CTM, you'll find a welcoming, team-oriented workplace that values diversity and compassion, where you can take pride in your work and the difference it makes.

title: Training Programme Director for Pathology Histapathology (London)
descriptionHtml:
An outstanding individual is sought to fulfil the role of Training Programme Director for Pathology Histopathology for London.

The role of Training Programme Director is to work with and support the Postgraduate Dean in leading the delivery of a wide range of functions within their specialty, aligned to the NHS England mandate. The Programme Director will ensure that both national standards, determined by the Royal College and also guidelines and standards established within Pathology Histopathology are met.

The successful applicant will work closely with the Head of School, other Pathology TPDs, LaSE team including; PGMDE Business Manager, Postgraduate Dean, and other key departments including Quality.

They will work with the Postgraduate Dean to produce doctors who will strive for the highest standards of patient-centred care and commit themselves to a lifetime of professional development.

The role ofTraining Programme Directoris to work with and support the Postgraduate Dean in leading the delivery of a wide range of functionswithin their specialty, aligned to theNHSEngland mandate.

A speciality Training Programme Director (TPD) is a member of the Speciality Training Committee (STC) who is managerially responsible to the Postgraduate Dean for the delivery of training in that speciality according to the standards set by the GMC and the Royal College of Pathology. The demands on TPDs are likely to vary at times and the guidance below should be interpreted flexibly.

NHS England has a wide range of statutory functions, responsibilities and regulatory powers. These are focused on supporting the wider NHS to deliver high quality care, as well as doing those things that are best done once for the whole NHS.

Our staff bring expertise across clinical, operational, commissioning, technology, data science, cyber security, software engineering, education, and commercial specialisms -- enabling us to design and deliver high-quality NHS services.

In March 2025, the Government announced that NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care will increasingly merge functions, ultimately leading to NHS England being fully integrated into the department.

If you currently work within the NHS and if successful at interview, we will initiate an Inter Authority Transfer (IAT) via the Electronic Staff Record (ESR).This retrieves key data from your current or previous NHS employer to support onboarding, including competency status, Continuous Service Dates (CSD), and annual leave entitlement. Colleagues with a contractual office base are expected to spend, on average, at least 40% of their time working in our offices.

employer: County Durham & Darlington NHS Foundation Trust
title: Clinical Specialist Doctor in Community Child Health
descriptionHtml:
Clinical Specialist Doctor in Community Child Health interest in Neurodevelopmental Paediatrics and Children in Care.

We are in the exciting position of being able to offer a clinical specialist post in the community and developmental paediatric service to an enthusiastic applicant with interests in neurodevelopmental paediatrics and the assessment of Children in Care. The post is for up to 10 Programmed Activities (10 PAs).

Clinical responsibility would be in a defined geographical patch within the Darlington and South Durham team who have bases at Darlington Memorial Hospital and Bishop Auckland General Hospital. However all staff are expected to work across Trust sites depending on the needs of the service.

The duties of these posts do not include any acute paediatric on call work.

The Community and Developmental Paediatrics Service provides consultant-led medical and health assessments, investigation, treatment, management and support for children and young people between the ages of 0-19 years in secondary care outpatient settings.

We work with children and young people with complex health needs resulting from neurological disorders affecting child development (neuro-disability), those with disordered child development or where there are concerns about developmental disorders, Special Educational Needs & Disability (SEND) and children and young people who are in care.

We are a dedicated team of highly specialised clinicians trained in paediatrics who have sub-specialised in community child health. We deliver holistic care as part of a multidisciplinary team with close links to primary care teams, 0-25 service, mental health providers, tertiary paediatrics and other hospital based paediatricians and agencies such as education, social care, public health and voluntary sector organisations.

If you are being interviewed you must accept an interview slot in the system to continue, even if you have arranged with the manager.

You must be able to produce ALL certificates stated essential in the person specification or you will not be able to complete pre-employment checks.

We provide hospital services from two acute sites - Darlington Memorial Hospital and University Hospital of North Durham. We have a centre for planned care in Bishop Auckland and provide care from community hospitals in Chester-le-Street, Shotley Bridge, Barnard Castle, Sedgefield and Weardale as well as over 80 other community based settings and providing care in patients' homes.

We particularly welcome applications from disabled and Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic (BAME) candidates as BAME and disabled people are currently under-represented.

Full Job Descriptions can be found in the adverts supporting documents.

Over reliance on AI-generated content is discouraged and may diminish the applicant's chances of success.

For the most up-to-date information on visa requirements and eligibility, please check online to determine whether you can apply.

Please note that we may close any vacancy early once a sufficient number of applications have been received.

title: General Practitioner for Urgent Treatment Centre
descriptionHtml:
Are you a GP looking for a role providing care for patients without the endless paperwork and administrative burden of traditional general practice?

We are seeking experienced General Practitioners to join our highly regarded Urgent Treatment Centre (UTC) on a substantive basis with availability of hours on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays. If regular hours are not suited to you but you are still interested in working for the UTC then we are also recruiting for bank opportunities.

We are a GP-led service providing assessment and management of a diverse mix of patients presenting with acute illnesses and urgent care needs. Working at the UTC offers an exciting opportunity to work within a supportive team delivering high-quality care to patients who need timely assessment and treatment, while maintaining an excellent work-life balance.

Join a supportive, experienced team where you can focus on delivering high-quality patient care. Enjoy a varied and interesting case mix, 20-minute appointments, and triage support, with minimal administrative burden beyond consultation records and referrals. We offer paid medical indemnity, 6 weeks' annual leave plus 1 week study leave (pro rata), NB Medical subscription, regular CPD opportunities, and flexible shift patterns including 6- and 12-hour shifts, with substantive and bank opportunities available.

GPs working at the UTC assess and manage patients presenting with a wide range of acute illnesses and urgent care needs. Patients are referred from the local Emergency Department (on the same site), local GP surgeries and NHS 111. The role offers genuine clinical variety while allowing you to concentrate on what matters most: delivering excellent patient care.

Our Urgent Treatment Centre is open 9am-9pm 365 days a year and sees approximately ~17,000 patients each year. It plays a vital role in reducing pressure on the local Emergency Department and General Practice. We are proud to consistently receive excellent patient feedback and maintain high patient satisfaction ratings as well as being well regarded by those who refer into the service.

What We're Looking For

  • GMC registered GP with a licence to practise
  • Experience managing acute and urgent presentations
  • Strong clinical decision-making skills
  • A team player committed to delivering high-quality patient-centred care
  • An interest in urgent care and service development

If you're passionate about providing excellent patient care, enjoy the variety and interesting case mix of working in an Urgent Care setting, have strong team-working values and want to join a service where your clinical expertise makes a real difference every day then wed love to hear from you.

If this opportunity is for you, please apply or to find out more or arrange an informal discussion please email Banbury UTC Clinical Lead: Rebecca.atterby@nhs.net.

PML is a successful not-for-profit, GP-led organisation providing various NHS community and primary care clinical services to patients across Oxfordshire and Northamptonshire. We have evolved as a NHS healthcare provider since 2004 and in the last few years have grown significantly, now employing around 300 staff with a turnover of c. £16m. PML holds GMS contracts, as well as being a GP Federation representing c. 50 GP practices covering approximately 650,000 patients.

For more information on PML and the services we provide, please visit our website at www.principal-medical.co.uk.

title: General Practitioner - HMP Lincoln
descriptionHtml:
Northamptonshire Healthcare Foundation Trust is recruiting General Practitioners (up to 8 sessions a week) to work at HMP Lincoln. This is a remand prison serving predominantly the population of Lincolnshire and North Nottinghamshire and the courts in Lincolnshire.

If you are interested in improving the lives of the most socially deprived population with complex health morbidities, then this job is for you. You will be providing physical healthcare equivalent to that in the community with fellow doctors and other healthcare professionals through a polyclinic model with expertise in Physical Health, Mental Health, Substance Misuse, Dentistry, Physiotherapy, Podiatry, Sexual Health etc. As such you will have quick access to all these specialists for your patients as opposed to the lengthy waiting times in community practices.

  • You will be a senior and experienced clinician who can work autonomously to a level of defined competencies, as agreed within local clinical governance frameworks.

    You will join an outstanding-rated Trust delivering trauma-informed healthcare within prisons, supported by strong medical leadership, protected CPD time and there may be an opportunity for some hybrid working. You may be asked to provide cross cover for GP colleagues at other prison sites within the Lincolnshire area. However, there are no on call commitments

    A typical working week is likely to include clinics/patient reviews, team meetings, liaison with other professionals, clinical administration, and supervision of clinical colleagues.

NHFT is an integrated primary care and mental health Trust, providing physical, mental health and specialty services in both hospital settings and out in the community. Because we put the person at the centre of all we do, we focus on delivering care that is as easy to access as possible. This means many of our services can be provided at home, work or in schools.We also provide health services to various prisons and detention centres in Bedfordshire and Cambridgeshire.

NHFT promotes a culture of learning to improve the care and safety of our patients and staff, which focuses on people who enable our Trust to be 'outstanding' by supporting opportunity, innovation, development and growth.

title: General Practice Based Pharmacist
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an experienced and motivated Clinical Pharmacist to join our multidisciplinary primary care team. The post holder will lead and develop medicines optimisation services within the practice, ensuring safe, effective, evidence-based, and cost-effective prescribing. The pharmacist will work collaboratively with GPs, the Practice Prescribing Lead, Pharmacy Technician, PCN Clinical Pharmacists, nursing staff, and administrative teams to improve patient outcomes and support delivery of high-quality care.

The successful candidate will play a key role in medication reviews, medicines reconciliation, safety monitoring, prescribing audits, medicines governance, CQC compliance, and medicines management processes. They will provide leadership to the practice pharmacy team and contribute to achieving national and local prescribing priorities.

  • Undertake structured medication reviews and medicines optimisation clinics for patients with long-term conditions, polypharmacy, frailty, learning disabilities, and other complex needs.
  • Review repeat prescribing processes to ensure safe and effective prescribing.
  • Support Medicines Reconciliation following hospital discharge and outpatient appointments.
  • Manage prescribing queries from patients, GPs, community pharmacies, care homes, and secondary care providers.
  • Identify and resolve medication-related problems and optimise treatment plans.
  • Promote adherence to local and national prescribing guidelines
  • Support high-risk medication monitor and chronic disease management

We offer the opportunity to join a forward-thinking and supportive GP practice where pharmacists play a central role in clinical care, medicines optimisation, patient safety, and service development. You will work closely with experienced GPs, the Prescribing Lead, Pharmacy Technician, and PCN pharmacy team to deliver high-quality patient-centred care and continuously improve prescribing and medicines management across the practice.

title: Support Worker
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a confident Care & Support Worker with a passion for delivering outstanding healthcare.

title: Pharmacist
descriptionHtml:
ClinicalPharmacist

Salary: £46,148

Hours: Full time 37.5 hrs per week

Must be a UK resident registered with the General Pharmaceutical Council

Site location:32 Clifton York

Manage and promote the repeat dispensing serviceRepeat prescription reauthorisation and acute prescription requestsMedication related queries from patients and staffIncrease safety mechanisms such as clinical audits

Implement MHRA drug withdrawals and alerts

Reduce inappropriate poly-pharmacy and wasteful prescribing through clinical medication review

employer: Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Healthcare for Older People and Stroke Medicine
descriptionHtml:
The Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is seeking to appoint a Consultant Physician in Healthcare for the Older Person and Stroke Medicine to join the department for its Northern services, based at North Devon District Hospital.

This is an exciting opportunity to join an established and dynamic team. Since North Devon District Hospital and the Royal Devon & Exeter Hospital merged in 2022 we have been able to provide additional clinical support and leadership to grow our services in our Northern site. This has allowed us to expand our multi-disciplinary workforce and introduce new services such as our front door frailty team and frailty acute hospital at home.

We are looking for enthusiastic, innovative and flexible individuals to further develop these services. North Devon has a large and increasing elderly population in a largely rural area with varying socio-economic needs. As such there is the opportunity to pursue sub-specialties tailored to the interests of the successful applicant. There is scope for working within frailty, ortho-geriatrics, movement disorders, syncope, stroke, community and peri-operative medicine.

A team of colleagues based in the Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital provide twice weekly cover at N

For more detail about the main duties of this role, please see the job description section below. As a key member of the Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, you will be joining an exceptional team working together to help our patients to stay healthy, when they need it most.

Stretching across Northern, Eastern and Mid Devon, we have a workforce of over 15,000 staff, making us the largest employer in Devon. Our core services, which we provide to more than 615,000 people, cover more than 2,000 square miles across Devon, while some of our specialist services cover the whole of the peninsula, extending our reach as far as Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly.

We deliver a wide range of emergency, specialist and general medical services through North Devon District Hospital and the Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital (Wonford).

Alongside our two acute hospitals, we provide integrated health and social care services across a variety of settings, including community inpatient hospitals, outpatient clinics, and within peoples own homes. We also offer primary care services, a range of specialist community services, and Sexual Assault Referral Centres (SARC).

Our state-of-the-art equipment, leading technologies and strong links to local universities put us at the forefront of research and innovations, enabling us to provide world-class care to our local communities.

Its never been a more exciting time to join the Royal Devon, as youll help to shape our services as we continue along our integration journey.

title: Clinical Fellow Ophthalmology
descriptionHtml:

The post holder will work with the current body of ophthalmology consultants at WEH and CXH in the ophthalmology directorate of Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust. The department is very busy, seeing over 5000 outpatients a month, and provides a tertiary referral service for West London.

There is a very active research unit: ICORG (Imperial College Ophthalmic Group) which is a part of Imperial College's department of Cancer and Surgery, and the team are actively participating in a number of phase 1 to phase 4 trials including surgical trials.

The post holder will work with the consultants and allied professionals in the emergency ophthalmology department which offers a 24 hour emergency service, 7 days a week to the local population and for complex referred emergency work. The WEH emergency ophthalmology team are part of the Imperial Trauma centre team.

Informal discussions/ visits to the Department are encouraged - to arrange please contact:

Mr Ahmed Alnahrawy , ED clinical lead, ahmed.alnahrawy@nhs.net

The post is 10 Clinical sessions across ED/ Cataract Surgery and general clinics

Candidate expected to have experience in Emergency ophthalmic and general ophthalmology

Experience in Cataract surgery

Medical Qualification MBBS or equivalent

Will carry out research/ audit and teaching

At Imperial College Healthcare you can achieve extraordinary things with extraordinary people, working with leading clinicians pushing boundaries in patient care.

Become part of a vibrant team living our values - expert, kind, collaborative and aspirational. You'll get an experience like no other and will fast forward your career.

Benefits include career development, flexible working and wellbeing, staff recognition scheme. Make use of optional benefits including Cycle to Work, car lease schemes, season ticket loan or membership options for onsite leisure facilities.

We are committed to equal opportunities and improving the working lives of our staff and will consider applications to work flexibly, part time or job share. Please talk to us at interview.

employer: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locally Employed Doctor Higher – Acute Frailty / Frailty Hub
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a Locally Employed Doctor (Higher) based within Acute Frailty Services and has been developed in partnership with the Clinical Service Lead for Healthcare of Older People. The post holder will join a dynamic multidisciplinary team delivering comprehensive geriatric assessment and frailty-focused care across acute and ambulatory settings. Each successful candidate will be allocated a named Educational Supervisor and supported in developing advanced skills in the assessment and management of older people living with frailty, complex multimorbidity, cognitive impairment, falls, and acute illness.

The post offers an excellent opportunity for doctors with an interest in Geriatric Medicine, Acute Frailty, Integrated Care, or General Internal Medicine who wish to develop higher-level competencies in the care of older adults. In addition to clinical training, there will be opportunities to participate in service development, quality improvement, teaching, leadership, and multidisciplinary working across the frailty pathway.

A comprehensive guide to all duties and responsibilities will be provided during induction and within the departmental handbook. Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

*To provide safe, effective, and compassionate care for older adults presenting with frailty, complex multimorbidity, cognitive impairment, falls, delirium, and acute medical illness across the Acute Frailty Hub, Frailty Same Day Emergency Care (FSDEC), OPAL service, and inpatient frailty wards.

*To undertake comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA), formulate management plans, and contribute to clinical decision-making in collaboration with consultants and the multidisciplinary team.

*To work within departmental, Trust, and national clinical guidelines, maintaining high standards of clinical governance and patient safety.

*To contribute to outpatient clinics and other clinical activities associated with the post, including sessions at Hodge Hill Primary Care Centre, as required by the agreed job plan and service needs.

*To provide clinical support to other areas within HCOP during periods of increased service pressure or staffing shortages, as reasonably required by the service.

*To liaise effectively with colleagues across the Emergency Department, specialty teams, primary care, community services, and social care providers to facilitate integrated and person-centred care.

*To maintain effective communication with patients, families, carers, and members of the multidisciplinary team

University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust strives to have an inclusive culture where everyone feels like they belong, can thrive, knows that they add value and feels valued. We do this by developing compassionate and culturally competent leaders, being values driven in all that we do and by creating a welcoming and inclusive workplace that thrives on the diversity of our people. As such we want to attract and recruit talented individuals from all backgrounds, and for each of you to feel supported for the diversity you bring, to achieve your full potential. For those staff with a disability, including physical disability, long term health condition, mental health or neurodiverse condition, this also means being committed to making reasonable adjustments needed for you to carry out your role.

title: Specialist Harm Reduction Worker
descriptionHtml:
Join our team as a Specialist Harm Reduction Worker in Fife on a permanent basis.

Are you a compassionate and motivated individual who wants to change peoples lives? Our team in Fife is looking for a Specialist Harm Reduction Worker to join them in providing high-quality recovery care to a diverse client group. If you are enthusiastic, creative and passionate about helping others, wed love to hear from you.

As a Specialist Harm Reduction Worker, we offer a starting salary of £26,250 per annum. The salary for this role is on an incremental scale and will rise each year in line with our pay progression salary bands, to £30,900 per annum. For further details please reach out to a member of the recruitment team via recruitment@wearewithyou.org.uk.

This is a full time, permanent position. This role will involve occasional evenings and weekend working.

Please refer to the linked job description to support your application.

The closing date for this role is 8th November 2026; however, please note that this role may close early should sufficient applications be received, so early application is advised. All applicants should submit a CV and a covering letter on why you would like to be considered for this role.

Our Specialist Harm Reduction Workers play a vital role in supporting clients, providing information and advice in relation to reducing drug and alcohol related harm, including promoting safer drug use practices; working with individuals most at risk.

In this role you will provide harm reduction interventions, structured one to one work, outreach harm reduction and multi agency liaison with our partners. You will play a key role in the development of Harm Minimisation interventions in a community setting.

This is a frontline role at WithYou, where you will provide continuity of care through effective partnership working, care coordination, key work responsibilities, and intervention delivery. You will manage an active caseload, connecting quickly with clients and ensuring theyre always treated with respect and dignity.

As a leading charity supporting people with drug, alcohol, and mental health challenges, we operate over 80 services across England and Scotland, providing free and confidential support to more than 100,000 people each year. WithYou is all about working with our clients to find the right path for them to get to where they want to be, and you will be joining an amazing team of people who go the extra mile to make that happen. Working within one of our services is always busy, sometimes challenging, but always rewarding.

WithYou provides free and confidential support, without judgement, to more than 100,000 people every year experiencing challenges with drugs, alcohol and mental health across England and Scotland.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
The Alexandra Partnership is seeking a dedicated and patient-focused Salaried General Practitioner to join our supportive and forward-thinking team.

This is a part-time opportunity (4 sessions per week), and candidates must be available to work on Mondays and Tuesdays.

  • Deliver high-quality, person-centred care across booked and same-day appointments

Sustainability is at the heart of our mission.
