title: Trust Doctor in Specialty and Integrated Medicine
descriptionHtml:
Do you have experience within the NHS in Acute, General and / or Elderly Medicine, having worked for at least 12-months in relevant posts including 6-months experience working at Registrar-level?

Applications are invited for two Registrar-level (ST3+ equivalent) Trust Doctor positions within the Specialty and Integrated Medicine Clinical Service Unit at Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust. The posts, which are available for immediate start and fixed term until 3rd August 2027, are ideally suited to resident doctors who have completed Internal Medicine Training (or equivalent) and are looking for more experience before entering a formal Higher Specialty Training programme.

Candidates must be fully registered with the General Medical Council and hold a license to practice by the intended start date.The successful applicants will help to cover all areas of our service, which include Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC), Acute Medical Units, and multiple in-patient Specialty Wards. Excellent training will therefore be provided in the management of acutely unwell and deteriorating patients, Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment, rehabilitation, and complex discharge planning. Out-of-hours, our Registrar-level doctors also contribute to the acute unselected take, providing experience in a broad range of general medical presentations.The Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust is committed to delivering the highest quality and safest treatment and care to every patient, every time.

Our vision is to provide the highest quality specialist and integrated care.

We will do this through delivery of our multi-year goals and strategic priorities, which you can read about on this page.

Central to it all is The Leeds Way  our values and behaviours that are at the heart of everything we do.

employer: Bradford Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant General & Upper GI Surgeon
descriptionHtml:
Bradford Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is looking to recruit a Consultant General & Upper GI Surgeon.

This is a permanent full time post (10 post).

Please note interview will be conducted face to face and no option of virtual interview.

The successful candidate will be expected to take up a post as a Consultant General & Upper GI Surgeon with a specialist interest in Bariatric and Benign UGI Surgery. This would include metabolic and weight loss surgery, management of complex hiatal conditions, and benign biliary surgery. Proficiency in advanced laparoscopic operating is essential. The UGI unit has access to Robotic surgery and the post holder could develop a robotic surgical practice.

As part of the department the post holder would be expected to provide assessment to outpatients with a wide variety of conditions and would be expected to partake in the triage and investigation of fast track referrals. The post holder would be expected to be Joint Advisory Group on Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (JAG) Accredited in Upper GI endoscopy.

The Gastrointestinal (GI) surgeons run the general surgical on call service (colorectal and upper gastrointestinal) which is currently a 1 in 14 rota. During periods on call the post holder will be freed up from all elective activity in order to run the surgical assessment unit and to triage and treat all acute surgical referrals. The post holder will also partake in a 1 in 14 rota to provide CEPOD acute operating lists and weekday hot clinics. Familiarity with the management of general surgical pathology, both upper and lower GI, would therefore be essential.

Our People Charter outlines the behaviours we can expect from one another and what you can expect from Bradford Teaching Hospitals Foundation Trust:

  • We value people
  • We are one team
  • We care

We're keen to meet people who share these values and are passionate about delivering the highest quality of care to our patients.

employer: Greater Manchester Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Trafford - Bolin & Greenway
descriptionHtml:
This is a well- established existing post and the postholder will provide medical leadership to the care of patients on Bollin (functional) and Greenway (organic) wards. There are a total of 21 patients on both wards.

In terms of medical support there are a Core Trainee trainee and Foundation Doctor allocated to work on the ward. There is 24 hour junior on-call support to the entire Moorside Unit. There is a ward manager and two deputy ward managers for each ward. In addition there is full complete of nursing staff, nursing assistants and a Support and Recovery Time Worker (STR). The ward has a psychologist, occupational therapist and physiotherapist. There are two physical health care nurses in the Moorside Unit who are able to provide input to the wards when required.

Clinical role

o Provide Medical leadership for MDT meetings.o Carry out comprehensive psychiatric Assessment and provide treatment for inpatients on the ward.o Support ward-based staff to manage psychiatric emergencieso Conduct patient reviews and lead Multidisciplinary ward reviews, CPA reviews and multi-professional meetings.o Be the responsible clinician for the purposes of the Mental Health Act 1983(amended 2007) and carry out duties in accordance to the code of practice.o Renew and maintain Responsible Clinician status according to agreed procedures.o Carry out comprehensive Risk Assessments and participate in Trust's risk management processes.o Provide medical leadership to the inpatient ward team.o Maintain a high level of effective communication and work flexibly and cooperatively with other parts of the service including other wards and inpatient units, community mental health teams, services and primary careo Liaison with Families and Carerso Complete reports for Mental Health Tribunals with the support of the Staff Grade doctoro Attend Mental Health Tribunals or supervise other members of the medical teams in Tribunal work Assess for use of the Mental Health Act, complete consent to treatment and authorise Section 17 leave.

Greater Manchester Mental Health (GMMH) Foundation Trust employs over 7000 members of staff, who deliver services from more than 122 locations.

We provide inpatient and community-based mental health care for people living in Bolton, the city of Manchester, Salford,Trafford and the borough of Wigan, and a wide range of specialist mental health and substance misuse services across Greater Manchester, the north west of England and beyond.

Greater Manchester is one of the world's most innovative, original and exciting places to live and work. From the beauty of the surrounding countryside to the heart of the vibrant inner city with great shopping, entertainment and dining options.

Wherever you go you will experience a great northern welcome with people famed for their warmth, humour and generosity.

Our people enjoy their work, have opportunities to learn and develop their skills and are encouraged to generate new ideas that improve care for our service users.

employer: Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust
title: Clinical Fellow in Paediatric Surgery and Urology
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a 6 to 12 months Clinical Fellow post in Paediatric Surgery department at Birmingham Children's Hospital, one of the busiest in the United Kingdom. The post will be on the Resident (1 in 8) tier of Paediatric Surgery and Urology on call rota (depending on the experience of the successful applicant). The role will be primarily for a Paediatric Urology Fellow who is near the end of their training (or has finished) but will involve cross-cover in Paediatric Surgery. Further details about the resident and non-resident tiers are provided below

The Department of Paediatric Surgery and Urology consist of 14 Consultant Paediatric Surgeons and Urologists. We serve a regional population of over 5 million, as well as receiving supra-regional referrals for complex cases. In addition, two Paediatric Hepatobiliary and Transplant surgeons provide their training expertise.

The placement offers exposure to a wide range of Paediatric Surgery and Urology at tertiary level. Successful Candidates will join the team on the Resident Registrar Tier on the Paediatric Surgery and Urology on call rota (please see job description for a description of the tiered rota).

Applicants should possess either the MBBS or recognised equivalent European equivalent.

Due to the nature of the position, the successful applicant will be required to undergo an enhanced DBS check.

Further information is available from Mr H Patel, Miss R Wragg, or Mr L McCarthy (0121 333 8110)

Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust is the first of its type in the UK. Our Trust was formed in February 2017 to drive forward our commitment to provide the highest quality, world-class physical and mental health care for our women, children and families. Uniting our hospitals means more seamless care; more investment to make greater advances in our specialist treatment and world-leading neo-natal and fetal work. Importantly, it also gives us a greater voice in shaping the future of family-centred care.

Birmingham Children's Hospital is a UK leading specialist paediatric centre with an international reputation in several areas.

Birmingham Women's Hospital is one of two dedicated women's hospitals in the UK, with the busiest single site maternity unit, delivering more than 8,200 babies a year offering a full range of gynaecological, maternity and neonatal care.

Our Trust is committed to creating the best place to work. We believe in promoting and enhancing inclusion, diversity and equality and encourage applications from all areas of the community, who meet the criteria for the role, regardless of age, gender identity, disability, race, religion or sexual orientation.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team
descriptionHtml:
We are recruiting for a full-time Consultant Psychiatrist to join ourCrisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team (CRHTT) based at Manzil Way in Oxford where you will have an active leadership role and medical responsibility for the diagnosis, management and treatment of adults of working age and older adults who are at risk of developing a mental health crisis.

With your expertise in Adult Psychiatry, you'll join our multi-disciplinary team (MDT) to deliver patient care through home treatment enabling early discharge from inpatient care. You'll work closely with inpatient wards and community teams, including the Inpatient Social Work service and the Patient Flow Transformation lead.

We offer rewarding career development with protected SPA time as part of your job plan, encouraging you to take leadership courses to enhance your skills. We also offer a relocation allowance of up to £8,000 for external applicants (subject to eligibility criteria).

Applicants must be fully registered with the General Medical Council (GMC) and on the Specialist Register or be within six months attaining their Certificate of Completion of Training (CCT) or an equivalent approved indicator of training.

Could this be the next step in your career? Come and join one of the UK's leading mental health Trusts at the forefront of research infrastructure and make a real difference to people's lives.

This role provides senior medical input and clinical leadership to the Oxfordshire Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team (CRHTT). You will have responsibility for your own patients as well as those patients seen by medical staff under your supervision.

The key components of the CRHTT service are:

1. Crisis response (emergency assessments and reviews)

2. Intensive home treatment characterized by the availability of multiple visits each day which are of a length and content to allow for specialist psycho-social intervention to be delivered

3. Gate-keeping admissions to psychiatric beds

4. Enabling early discharge from psychiatric admission

OHFT mental health urgent care works in close collaboration with other community mental health provision, Inpatient Services and wider system partners including Thames Valley Police, South Central Ambulance Service, the Oxfordshire Mental Health Partnership (OMHP) organisations (Response, Mind, Elmore, Connections and Restore), Oxford University Hospitals NHS FT and primary care services. CRHTT services are now widespread across the UK and provide a genuine alternative to hospital care and treatment.

Oxford Health is a great place to work and to be able to showcase the best of yourself when making an application please read the "candidate guide to making an application" and ensure your supporting statement is tailored to the role you are applying for and addresses any essential criteria.As a Trust we provide physical, mental health and social care for people of all ages across Oxfordshire, Buckinghamshire, Swindon, Wiltshire, Bath and Northeast Somerset. Our services are delivered at community bases, hospitals, clinics and people's homes, delivering care as close to home as possible. Our vision is that no matter who you are or where you are, you will tell us that you receive: "Outstanding care delivered by an outstanding team"Our values are: "Caring, safe and excellent"We offer a wide range of benefits designed to support your career and wellbeing. These include:o Excellent opportunities for career progressiono Access to tailored individual and Trust wide learning and developmento 33 days annual leave per annum/pro-rata increasing to 35 days after seven years seniorityo NHS Discount across a wide range of shops, restaurants and retailerso Competitive pension schemeo Lease car schemeo Cycle to work schemeo Employee Assistance Programmeo Mental Health First Aiderso Staff accommodation (please note waiting lists apply)o Staff networking and support groups hosted by our Equality, Diversity & Inclusion team

employer: London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust
title: Specialty Registrar- Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery
descriptionHtml:
This is an exciting opportunity to join a fast paced, challenging and busy specialty to improve understanding and experience in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery. These appointments are initially for 12 months and will be based mainly at Northwick Park Hospital. It requires motivated doctors with some Oral & Maxillofacial surgery experience to work with other trainee doctors and consultants to care for the emergency and elective patients within OMFS and Head & Neck. A broad based knowledge in all aspects of OMFS is beneficial but the weekly timetable can be adjusted considering the experience of the successful candidate and the need of the service.

The successful candidate will work as a member of the middle grade team who all are both medically and dentally qualified doctors supporting services across the network and participating in 2nd call rota.

OMFS ServiceThe London North West Regional Maxillofacial Unit opened its doors at Northwick Park Hospital in May 2006. This is a Specialist Regional In-Patient Service with dedicated nursing and Critical Care support. In addition there is a prosthodontic and vibrant regional orthodontic service.There is a state of the art maxillofacial and orthodontic laboratory, administrative wing and offices for Oral & Maxillofacial consultants, secretaries and junior doctors. Outpatients facilities are of the latest designs and have PACs associated oral and facial imaging equipment including X-ray and ultrasound imaging and facilities for nasendoscopy.

London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust (LNWH) cares for the people of Brent, Ealing, Harrow and beyond.

Our team of more than 8,200 clinical and support staff serve a diverse population of almost one million people.

We run major acute services at:

  • Northwick Park Hospital: home to one of the busiest emergency departments (A&E) in the country. The hospital provides a full range of services including the country's top-rated hyper-acute stroke unit and one of only three hyper-acute rehabilitation units in the UK
  • St Mark's Hospital: an internationally renowned specialist centre for bowel disease
  • Ealing Hospital: a busy district general hospital providing a range of clinical services, as well as 24/7 emergency department and urgent care centre, and specialist care at Meadow House Hospice
  • Central Middlesex Hospital: our planned care site, hosting a range of surgical and outpatient services and collocated with an urgent care centre.

We are a university teaching NHS trust, in recognition of the important role we play in training clinicians of the future and bringing the benefits of research to the public.

employer: Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Rheumatology
descriptionHtml:
Working Part time: 7 Sessions hours per week

We are looking to recruit a Substantive Consultant in Rheumatology, and we are open to incorporating any specialist interests and developed skills within the job plan. The successful candidate will be a part-time appointment working 3.5 days in Rheumatology, which is a growing department with a dynamic and flexible team of enthusiastic consultants and specialist practitioners. employer: The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Senior Clinical Fellow in Advanced Heart Failure, Transplant & MCS
descriptionHtml:
We are delighted to be able to offer an opportunity for a highly motivated, ambitious individual to join our well integrated team.

This post is an exciting opportunity for postgraduate trainees in Cardiology to gain extensive experience and participate in the outpatient and inpatient multi-disciplinary assessment, diagnosis, and treatment of patients with advanced heart failure including heart transplant and mechanical circulatory support.

Please read attached Job Description and Person Specification.

employer: Calderdale and Huddersfield NHS Foundation Trust
title: Specialty Doctor in Emergency Medicine and Urgent Care
descriptionHtml:
We are inviting applications in the Emergency Medicine Department at Calderdale and Huddersfield NHS Foundation Trust for Trust doctors at Registrar.

The role will be an entirely clinical role at middle grade level within the department and the successful candidate will work with the current team in supporting and developing the department. Calderdale and Huddersfield NHS Foundation Trust is heavily invested in providing an excellent Urgent and Emergency Care system for our population. We are looking to recruit motivated and enthusiastic doctors to provide care in the Emergency Departments and/or our Urgent SDEC (uSDEC)

The Emergency Departments at Calderdale Royal Hospital and Huddersfield Royal Infirmary are currently led by 23 consultants who work across both sites providing 16hr shop-floor cover 7 days a week at both sites and on-call cover beyond that. Specialty Doctors, Higher Specialty Trainees and ST3+ grade doctors provide 24 hour shop-floor cover at both sites.

There is a consultant led Trauma Team at Huddersfield, which has been designated as a Major Trauma Unit in the West Yorkshire Regional Trauma Network. Both Huddersfield and Calderdale have 4 resuscitation bays, including a dedicated paediatric resus area, with X-ray and ultrasound facilities. There are separate majors and minors areas with a play-room available for Families with Younger Children in both departments.

Successful candidates will be involved in the design and delivery of these exciting new additions to regional Emergency Services. As a speciality doctor in the ED we are dedicated to developing you and your interests. Depending on your interests and performance we have various programs we can support including entry on to our CESR program (from which previous candidates have been appointed as consultants)

We employ more than 6,500 staffwho deliver compassionate care from our two main hospitals,Calderdale Royal Hospital and Huddersfield Royal Infirmary as well as in community sites, healthcentres and in patients' homes. We also are incredibly proud to have almost 150 volunteers here at CHFT.

We provide a range of services including urgent and emergency care; medical; surgical; maternity; gynaecology; critical care; children's and young people's services; end of life care and outpatient and diagnostic imaging services.

We provide community health services, including sexual health services in Calderdale from Calderdale Royal and local health centres. These include Todmorden Health Centre and Broad Street Plaza.

We continue to modernise and invest in our health services to build on our strong reputation.Foundation trusts are public leaders in improving quality in health services. They are part of the NHS- yet decisions about what they do and how they do it are driven by independent boards. Boardslisten to their Council of Governors and respond to the needs of their members - patients, staff andthe local community.

Foundation trusts provide what the health service wants, yet are also free to invest quickly in thechanges to the local community needs, in striving to be the best, and in putting their patients first.

employer: Cambridge University Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Anaesthetist with interest in Transplant Anaesthesia
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for the post of Consultant Anaesthetist with interest in Transplant Anaesthesia, based at Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge.

Interviews for this post will be held in person on 08 December 2026 at Addenbrooke's Hospital, Hills Road, Cambridge CB2 0QQ.

The successful candidate will join a team of 12 Transplant Anaesthetists covering a dedicated 24/7 transplant on call rota. Our transplant numbers have seen a year-on-year increase for the last five years. At present, we perform 100-120 liver, 10-15 multivisceral, 10-15 pancreas and 150-200 kidney transplants per year. We are actively involved in the research program into organ optimisation using normothermic machine perfusion (NMP) and normothermic regional perfusion (NRP). This post will include sessions in other surgical subspecialties according to mutually agreed job planning. The on call commitment will be for transplant and Post Anaesthesia Care Unit (PACU) rota.

The candidate must be fully registered with the GMC and would be expected to be on the GMC Specialist Register or within 6 months of their expected date of receipt of a CCT at the time of interview. Applications are welcomed from those unable to work full time for personal reasons or those wishing to job-share.

The applicant must have demonstrable skills in listening, reading, writing and speaking in English that enable effective communication about medical topics with patients and colleagues, as set out in the GMC's Good Medical Practice (2013). Non-UK applicants must possess the IELTS/OET exam before obtaining a GMC licence to practice.

Applications from job seekers who require skilled worker sponsorship to work in the UK are welcome and will be considered alongside all other applications. For further information please visit the UK Visas and Immigration website.

It is a requirement for skilled worker applicants, applying for entry clearance into the UK, to present a criminal record certificate from each country they have resided continuously or cumulatively for 12 months or more in the past 10 years. Adult dependants (over 18 years old) will also be subject to this requirement.

Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is an Equal Opportunities Employer.

title: Salaried GP Role
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to recruit a qualified GP for 6 sessions per week.

This role is supported with the help of the GP Practice Level reimbursement scheme. 4 Sessions are paid for by the practice and 2 sessions from the ICB. The position of 6 sessions will remain as long as the schemes runs by the ICB.

You would be joining a supportive, high-performing, and friendly team who are passionate about delivering modern, efficient primary care while maintaining the traditional values of general practice.

Our surgery provides an excellent working environment for both patients and staff. We serve a practice population of over 10200 patients.

We offer 10-minute consultations and have a low home visit rate.

We have 2 GP Trainers on site, and we regularly host F2 and ST trainees. We embrace new technologies and innovations to support accessible, high-quality care.

Provide high-quality patient care

Conduct surgery and telephone clinic, plus occasional home visits

Liaise with colleagues and external providers to ensure seamless care

Investigate and refer patients appropriately, in line with guidance

Review results and correspondence promptly

Provide cover for colleagues when required

Collect and review data for audit and QOF purposes

Maintain excellent communication with patients and carers

Attend clinical, governance, and educational meetings

Work collaboratively and effectively within the team

Manage your own workload and resources effectively

Attend required training events and feedback sessions

Report and follow up on significant incidents

About us

  • GMS Practice with 10230 + patients
  • No Extended Hours Commitment

title: Consultant OMFS / Maxillofacial Surgeon
descriptionHtml:
Medinet are seeking experienced Consultant Oral and Maxillofacial (OMFS) Surgeons to support services at Huddersfield Royal Infirmary.

This is an excellent opportunity for suitably qualified consultants to support outpatient clinics and minor operations, helping to manage patient demand and deliver timely specialist care for adult patients.

Working pattern: Monday - Friday

Hours: 7:30am - 6:00pm

The role will involve a combination of outpatient clinics and minor operations (MOPs), seeing approximately 24 adult patients per day in outpatient clinics and 8-10 patients per day for minor operations. Skin procedures will be performed under local anaesthetic and will primarily involve skin cancers and lesions of the head and neck, including the scalp, ears, nose and lips. The role will include the excision of basal cell carcinomas (BCCs) and squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs), with skin grafts or flap reconstruction undertaken where clinically required and within the consultants competence. Responsibilities will also include reviewing investigation results, preparing result letters and dictating correspondence for benign findings, with access to remote systems where available. The consultant will support fast-track oral patients throughout the clinical pathway, from initial consultant assessment and onward procedures through to the subsequent review of results.

Medinet is a leading UK provider of specialist clinical services, working in partnership with NHS organisations to increase clinical capacity, reduce waiting lists and improve patient access to high-quality care.

With over 20 years of experience supporting the NHS, Medinet delivers flexible insourcing services across a broad range of elective specialties. Our services are designed around the individual requirements of NHS Trusts, utilising existing hospital facilities and providing experienced clinical teams to deliver additional activity safely and efficiently.

Medinet has a network of more than 6,000 registered clinicians across the UK, supported by a dedicated full-time clinical team providing governance, assurance and oversight of service delivery.

title: Locum Consultant Neonatologist
descriptionHtml:

NICU Service

employer: University Hospitals Dorset NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Cardiologist with specialist interest Coronary Intervention
descriptionHtml:
Applications are being sought for the post of Consultant Cardiologist with a specialist interest in Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) at University Hospitals Dorset NHS Foundation Trust (UHD). The candidate will join the team of 7 (5 full time and 2 part time) Coronary Interventionalists based at the Dorset Heart Centre. The post has been developed to support the PCI service in view of two Interventional Cardiologists taking partial retirement and now covering a single position on the primary PCI on-call rota. There are no general medical commitments. You must have (or be within 6 months of obtaining) a CCT in cardiology.

As part of our commitment to delivering high-quality care across seven days, this post may involve participation in an out-of-hours rota, including evenings, weekends, and/or bank holidays, in accordance with service needs. Any work undertaken outside standard hours/PA's will attract remuneration in line with the respective NHS Medical and Dental Terms and Conditions of Service.

The busy PCI service covers Dorset, and adjacent parts of Hampshire and Wiltshire, a catchment of approx. 1 million.

The current PCI volume is approximately 1500 cases per year which includes up to 400 primary PCI treated through a 24/7 service.We employ all standard and advanced PCI techniques.This includes multi-vendor pressure wire, and imaging with integrated intravascular ultrasound (Philips & Boston) and optical coherence tomography (OCT). We have a full range of strategies for calcium modification including rotational, laser and orbital atherectomy and intravascular lithotripsy. There is a CTO programme and access to mechanical circulatory support with Impella.

We have extensive experience of bifurcation PCI including left main and had a long association with dedicated stent programmes. We have an affiliation with the European Bifurcation Club. Many patients are recruited into international clinical trials of PCI techniques, strategies and devices. Indeed, the unit has developed a reputation for high volume enrolment, subject retention and provision of excellent quality data.

UHD are investing, developing and transforming Trust services in line with the New Hospital Programme. As part of this, some services may move site this year or next, either temporarily or permanently. Recruiting Managers will be happy to answer any service-specific questions at interview.

If a role or service relocates as part of a planned move, excess mileage will not be reimbursed. Travel from home to the new work base will be classed as a normal commute. Any other changes will be managed under Trust or national terms and conditions.

UHD has active networks including Women's, BAME, Pride, EU, Pro Ability, and Armed Forces. We support Disability Confident and Armed Forces Covenant interview schemes.

AI tools may be used, but applications must honestly reflect your own skills and experience. Integrity is key to our recruitment process.

We do reserve the right to close this advertisement early if we receive a high volume of suitable applications

title: Bank Endoscopy Nurse
descriptionHtml:
UNLOCK YOUR BEST WORK LIFE

+ make a difference for every patient

Are you a motivated and experienced Registered Nurse with Endoscopy experience looking for flexible working opportunities? We are looking for a Bank Endoscopy Nurse to join our dedicated team at Practice Plus Group Hospital Ilford.

This is an excellent opportunity to work within a modern, patient-focused Endoscopy service, supporting patients throughout their journey while enjoying the flexibility that bank work offers. Whether you're looking to supplement your current role or gain additional experience, you'll be part of a professional and supportive team committed to delivering outstanding care.

As our Bank Endoscopy Nurse, you'll be responsible for assessing patient care needs, planning and delivering high-quality nursing care, and supporting patients before, during and after endoscopy procedures.

Working as part of a multidisciplinary team, you'll rotate across different areas of the Endoscopy Department, including procedure rooms, pre-assessment and recovery. You'll play a key role in ensuring patients receive safe, compassionate and effective care while maintaining the highest clinical standards.

This role is offered on a bank (0-hour) contract. There are no guaranteed hours, and shifts will be offered depending on business needs. You can accept or decline shifts based on your availability, making this a flexible optionbut it may not be suitable if you are seeking consistent or full-time hours.

As our Bank Endoscopy Nurse, you will be:

  • Delivering safe, individualised nursing care to Endoscopy patients.
  • Assessing, planning, implementing and evaluating patient care.
  • Supporting patients undergoing both sedated and non-sedated procedures.
  • Providing pre and post-procedure advice and patient education.
  • Working across procedure rooms, recovery and pre-assessment services.
  • Maintaining accurate patient records using clinical systems and documentation processes.
  • Supporting safe medication management in line with hospital policies.
  • Contributing to clinical governance, audit and quality improvement activities.
  • Supporting colleagues, students and junior team members within the department.
  •  Ensuring compliance with JAG standards and best practice guidance. 

As a registered nurse with relevant experience working endoscopy, you will also have:  

  • Evidence of ongoing personal and professional development.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to prioritise workload effectively.
  • Evidence of competence within Endoscopy practice.
  • Commitment to delivering high-quality patient care.
  • Flexible approach to working patterns and service requirements.
  • Theatre practitioner experience - desirable.
  • Understanding of quality, governance and regulatory requirements within Endoscopy services - desirable.
  • Awareness of the Care Standards Act and current best practice guidance - desirable.

What you can expect in return;

  • A bank rate of £22.98 per hour
  • Flexible shifts to suit your availability
  • Opportunity to work within a high performing clinical team
  • Supportive working environment focused on quality patient care

To apply for the role, click on the link below. If you have any questions, contact sarah.melder@practiceplusgroup.com 

Applications will be processed at the time of application, Practice Plus Group therefore reserves the right to close the advertisement before the stated closing date for that reason it is encouraged that you do not delay in your application.

Our employment offers are subject to receipt of satisfactory pre-employment checks. At Practice Plus Group, we actively promote diversity and equal opportunities.

Applicants must have the right to work in the UK.

employer: University Hospital of North Midlands NHS Trust
title: Locum Consultant Musculoskeletal Radiologist
descriptionHtml:
The post holder will join a team of 5.5 WTE musculoskeletal radiology consultants. Their duties will include providing a comprehensive diagnostic and interventional musculoskeletal imaging service across the Trust. The post holder should be a dedicated clinician wishing to actively assist and further develop Musculoskeletal Radiology services in the Trust.

The post holder will join a team of of 48 WTE Consultant Radiologists and will provide MSK, diagnostic and interventional radiology services to Trauma & Orthopaedics, Spine and Rheumatology Directorates.

The skill mix is well established within MSK and currently we have a large number of advanced practitioners and consultant radiographers who report plain films, sonographers who perform and report MSK diagnostic US examinations and an advanced practitioner who reports knee and spine MRI exams.

As a Locum MSK consultant radiologist at UHNM you will be working with some of the latest equipment available in a purpose built department. A new hospital complex at the Royal Stoke University Hospital opened in March 2012 and provides high quality imaging equipment. In January 2017 a dedicated IR Day Case Unit with 8 beds and IR clinic facilities was built within the IR department. Overall the Imaging department has seven MRI scanners, a mobile MRI and nine CT scanners on both sites plus 2 ED scanners in ED - one of which is a dual energy Siemens Force.

At UHNM the MSK radiologists work closely with their colleagues through cancer MDTs and joint clinico-radiological conferences. The successful applicant will share responsibilities to support the Trauma and orthopaedics, Spinal and Rheumatology Directorates through Multi-Disciplinary team meetings. Currently Spine, Rheumatology, Diabetes, Orthopaedic and Tumour MDTMs are in place and there is a rota for a lead radiologist for each of them.

The post holder will contribute to thedelivery of a high quality radiology servicewithin a busy imaging department providing both general and specialist services in diagnostics and interventional imaging which performs more than 700,000 Imaging examinations and procedures per year.

The post-holder will contribute to the weekday on-call service on rotation with also a 1 in 8 rota for Saturdays or Sundays.

The job plan will include CPD SPA

We are the specialist centre for major trauma for the North Midlands and North Wales. Happy staff make for happy patients, and with the help of both we have put together a wide range of development and support packages aimed at ensuring that everyone at the Trust has the opportunity to fulfil their potential and meet their aspirations as well as the tools to provide great care.

UHNM is a tertiary referral centre for Trauma and Orthopaedics, supported by a team of 29 Orthopaedic surgeons, taking in a population of approximately 1.5 million from Shropshire, Staffordshire, South Cheshire and Wolverhampton. The spinal team has 9 dedicated Spine surgeons providing all aspects of trauma and orthopaedics and spinal services including deformity correction, oncology surgery and trauma. There is a huge demand for MSK intervention services from these directorates for procedures including image guided injections, arthrography, myelography, biopsies, nerve root blocks and vertebroplasty and the post holder is expected to contribute to this type of work.

The Haywood Hospital has specialist services for rheumatology and rehabilitation. The Rheumatology centre at the Haywood Hospital welcomes patients from North Staffordshire, Derbyshire and Cheshire. The Haywood hospital is a centre of excellence and has an active research team known nationally and internationally for its work.

employer: Tees Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist in Community AMH
descriptionHtml:
The Harrogate & Ripon locality is covered by two community mental health teams: Harrogate Integrated Community team (HICT) and Ripon Integrated Community Team (RICT) now merged. These teams include workers with assertive outreach and primary care functions, hence the term Integrated. They are both based at Hummingbird House, 31-33 Victoria Ave, HG1 5QE in Harrogate. The post holder will be expected to provide medical leadership to the Harrogate Community Mental Health Team and support Ripon Community Mental Health Team.

HICT covers the areas of Harrogate and Wetherby. Consultants for crisis team, The Orchards, perinatal, EIP and eating disorders work less than full time supported by community consultants.

The postholder has dedicated admin support, including individual office space and access to PC/laptop/phone with easy access to IT support if required. This is in line with RCPsych recommendations for Consultant Psychiatrists office space and support. They also have dedicated time in their work schedule within which to complete their assigned clinical duties, including those on Community Treatment Orders (CTO). The post holder will have an average of 8 patients on CTO/MOJ.

You will provide consultant lead in line with the principles of New Ways of Working. The team works on principles of productive and purposeful community services (PPCS). This approach to community care provides increase meaningful clinical activity and ensures evidence-based care in a way that reduces patient journey times and waste. Key elements of PPCS are in place and include the use of clinical huddles and clinical leadership teams in key decision-making and the need for more assertive caseload review and management processes. This occurs through incorporating early senior input into patient formulation and care as well as hosting regular reviews which allows clear and early decision-making. The core clinical work will involve outpatient clinics, formulation, review and leadership meetings and Mental Health Act-related work. The direct clinical workload centres on one new-patient clinic (2-3) patients weekly and two follow-up clinics weekly (5-6 patients each) approximately. Assessment of new patients and review of old ones will be according to need, as may be requested by their different care co-ordinators or the leadership team.

Based on Royal College recommendations, Outpatient work will comprise 3.5 PAs; Clinical Admin 1 PA; MDT work 1 PA; Emergencies 1 PA and MHA work 0.5 PAs. There will be flexibility around this guide depending on team requirements and support.

Further information can be found in the attached Job Description.

We are one of the largest specialist mental health and learning disabilities trusts in the country operating from sites in Durham, Teesside, North Yorkshire and York and Selby. We provide a range inpatient and community services to people living in County Durham, the Tees Valley, Scarborough, Whitby, Ryedale, Harrogate, Hambleton and Richmondshire. We also provide additional specialist services to other parts of Northern England.

We deliver our services by working in partnership with eight local authorities and clinical commissioning groups, a wide range of voluntary organisations, as well as service users, their carers and the public.

Psychiatrists are essential contributors to our mental health teams. Service users expect and are justified to expect collaborative relationships with dedicated psychiatrists who work consistently as part of effective services. The Medical Directorate and Medical Development Team are striving to improve medical workforce recruitment and retention in a variety of ways and the cornerstone of these efforts is The TEWV Charter for the Medical Workforce. (Please see attached Supporting Document).

title: Consultant in Rheumatology
descriptionHtml:
The appointee will join the well-established department of eight existing consultants in rheumatology. This post will be Cross site between Bedford and Luton Sites. The successful candidate will augment and complement the consultant capacity, to help drive forwards the department's vision of a comprehensive rheumatology service. Sub-specialty interest in any area appropriate for a DGH (such as vasculitis, bone health or axial spondyloarthritis) is welcomed, as is an enthusiasm for teaching, audit and research.

The post holders will work with the other Consultants to provide specialty rheumatology advice and support to patients within the Trust. They will attend the weekly multi-disciplinary departmental meetings and weekly X-ray meetings, and will be expected to help support and train the registrars and other junior medical staff in rheumatology/general medicine, and the Clinical Nurse Specialists.

Where possible, the post-holder will be encouraged to develop a research interest, compatible with the background of the department and its facilities. Audit will be a mandatory part of the role.

The Rheumatology Directorate has close links with local General Practitioners and there is an active teaching program for them, and also for all grades of doctors within the Trust. The post holder will be encouraged to continue teaching and training at all levels.

Clinical Governance and Audit projects are undertaken as an ongoing programme within the department of Rheumatology - examining local practice compared to National Standards of care (for example use of biologic therapy, DAS scoring, early arthritis pathways and comparison to BSR Standards) - and Trust-wide. It is expected that the appointee will be actively involved in this.

Bedfordshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust provides hospital services to a growing population of around 700,000 people living across Bedfordshire and the surrounding areas across two busy hospital sites in Bedford and Luton. Both hospital sites offer key services such as A&E, Obstetrics-led Maternity and Paediatrics. You will be joining a friendly, high performing Trust committed to ensuring the health and wellbeing of staff. As one of the largest NHS Trusts in our region you will have access to a programme of high quality training and development to help you grow your career. The Trust continues to be committed to delivering the best patient care using the best clinical knowledge and technology.

Our Values

We not only recruit based on qualifications and experience - we recruit individuals who demonstrate the behaviours which underpin our Trusts core values. We achieve this by using values based recruitment. We are dedicated to making our recruitment practices as inclusive as possible for everyone, we are committed to promoting equality and diversity, and creating a culture that values differences.

title: Consultant - Gastroenterologist
descriptionHtml:
Applicants are invited to apply for an exciting Consultant Gastroenterologist opportunity at Royal Cornwall Hospitals NHS Trust, based in the cathedral city of Truro. This is an excellent opportunity to join a dynamic and supportive department delivering high-quality clinical care, education, research and innovation.

The successful candidate will join a team of nine Gastroenterologists and four Hepatologists serving a population of approximately 580,000. The department has benefited from significant investment, including a £3.4 million redevelopment of the Endoscopy Unit, which includes seven procedure rooms and supports a comprehensive endoscopy service.

The service provides advanced endoscopy including EMR, ESD, ERCP, EUS, capsule endoscopy and bowel cancer screening. We also deliver specialist services in IBD, nutrition, hepatology and complex polyp management, supported by experienced multidisciplinary teams and specialist nursing staff.

Applications are welcomed from clinicians with interests in advanced endoscopy, IBD, nutrition, hepatology, education, research, digital innovation or service development. Opportunities exist to undertake leadership, teaching and quality improvement activities.

Cornwall offers an exceptional quality of life, combining stunning coastline, beautiful countryside and excellent leisure opportunities with the chance to build a rewarding consultant career.

The successful candidate will play a central role in the continued development of gastroenterology services at Royal Cornwall Hospitals NHS Trust.

The job will entail:

Outpatients care - clinics (usually 2 a week), endoscopy lists (usually 2 a week)

Inpatient care - 1 in 9 ward weeks, 1 in 9 endoscopy on call, GiM post take ward round (3.5 hr evening ward round approx 1 in 18 weekdays only. No overnight or weekend GiM commitment)

Teaching - undergraduate and post graduate teaching (with opportunities to expand this if interested)

Attendance at MDTs and governance meetings

Personal development and leaderships opportunities if desired

Research opportunities if desired

Royal Cornwall Hospitals NHS Trust is the principal provider of acute and specialist healthcare services for Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly, serving a population of approximately 580,000 people. Services are delivered across Royal Cornwall Hospital in Truro, St Michael's Hospital in Hayle and West Cornwall Hospital in Penzance, alongside a range of community-based services.

The Trust provides a comprehensive range of acute and specialist care and works closely with partners across the health and care system to deliver high-quality, patient-centred services and improve outcomes for local communities.

As a teaching hospital and partner of the University of Exeter Medical School, the Trust has a strong reputation for education, training and research. Staff benefit from opportunities in leadership, teaching, innovation and clinical research, supported by continued investment in facilities, technology and service development.

Cornwall offers an outstanding quality of life, with dramatic coastline, beautiful countryside, excellent schools and thriving communities. Combined with strong transport links and extensive outdoor leisure opportunities, it provides an ideal location in which to build both a successful career and rewarding lifestyle.

title: Advanced Medical Practitioner - Care Homes
descriptionHtml:
South Doc Services (SDS) is hiring an Advanced Medical Practitioner (AMP) on behalf of West Heath Surgery.

This will be a full time, permanent role with a 37.5 hours per week contract arrangement. The job location is at West Heath Surgery, 194 - 196 West Heath Road, Birmingham, B31 3HB. Pay / Salary is dependent on experience level.

If you wish to have the full job description, please email rhiannon.aiken@nhs.net

The Advanced Medical Practitioner (AMP) will provide high-quality, safe, effective and person-centred clinical care to patients registered with West Heath Surgery who reside in designated care homes.

The post-holder will work as an integral member of the Practice multidisciplinary team, working collaboratively with GPs, advanced practitioners, practice nurses, clinical pharmacists, community nurses, therapists, care coordinators, social care professionals, care-home staff and other relevant health and social care professionals.

The post-holder will contribute to the delivery of proactive, personalised and coordinated healthcare for care-home residents, with an emphasis on:

  • prevention of avoidable deterioration;
  • early identification and management of acute illness;
  • proactive management of frailty and long-term conditions;
  • personalised care and support planning;
  • medicines optimisation in collaboration with the appropriate prescriber/pharmacy professional;
  • reducing avoidable hospital admissions;
  • facilitating timely access to secondary and community care;
  • supporting residents to remain in their preferred place of care wherever clinically appropriate;
  • effective multidisciplinary working;
  • continuity and coordination of care; and
  • safe, evidence-based clinical decision-making.

The role will support the Practice in delivering its contractual requirements under the current NHS England Network Contract DES and Enhanced Health in Care Homes arrangements. The current EHCH model is designed around proactive, personalised and integrated care for people living in care homes rather than a predominantly reactive model.

The post-holder will work within their individual scope of professional practice, competence and authority. Where an activity requires GP, consultant, specialist or other professional input, the AMP will recognise this promptly and escalate appropriately.

title: Training Programme Director - Emergency Medicine (South London)
descriptionHtml:
An outstanding individual or individuals is sought to fulfil the role of Training Programme Director for Emergency Medicine (South London).

The role of Training Programme Director is to work with and support the Postgraduate Dean in leading the delivery of a wide range of functions within their specialty, aligned to the NHS England mandate. The Programme Director will ensure that both national standards, determined by the Royal College and also guidelines and standards established within Emergency Medicine are met.

The successful applicant will work closely with the Head of School, other Medicine TPDs, LaSE team including; PGMDE Business Manager, Postgraduate Dean, and other key departments including Quality.

They will work with the Postgraduate Dean to produce doctors who will strive for the highest standards of patient-centred care and commit themselves to a lifetime of professional development.

The Programme Director will ensure that both national standards, determined by the Royal College, and guidelines and standards established within Emergency Medicine are met. Responsibilities will include:

  • To oversee the Specialty's Regional Training Programme
  • Specialty-specific matters and trainee/trainer concerns
  • Recruitment to training posts and programmes
  • Postgraduate programme management, including assessments, progression, rotations, support and remediation, OOP management, trainee management careers support, less than full-time training, inter-deanery transfer, academic training and other related work-streams.

The ideal candidate will be an experienced NHS Consultant with a thorough understanding of Emergency Medicine training across the region and who will also have strong leadership and communication skills and be able to work effectively as a member of a multi-professional team.

NHS England has a wide range of statutory functions, responsibilities and regulatory powers. These are focused on supporting the wider NHS to deliver high quality care, as well as doing those things that are best done once for the whole NHS.

Our staff bring expertise across clinical, operational, commissioning, technology, data science, cyber security, software engineering, education, and commercial specialisms -- enabling us to design and deliver high-quality NHS services.

In March 2025, the Government announced that NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care will increasingly merge functions, ultimately leading to NHS England being fully integrated into the department.

If you currently work within the NHS and if successful at interview, we will initiate an Inter Authority Transfer (IAT) via the Electronic Staff Record (ESR).This retrieves key data from your current or previous NHS employer to support onboarding, including competency status, Continuous Service Dates (CSD), and annual leave entitlement. You may opt out at any stage of the process.

Colleagues with a contractual office base are expected to spend, on average, at least 40% of their time working in our offices.

We cannot offer visa sponsorship for any vacancies.

employer: Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

Responsible for the timely review of all medical patients attending the services.

Daily ward rounds and identifying morning discharges ensuring the patient is safely discharged from the department.

Administrative duties within the department.

Management of the department to maintain efficient and timely patient flow with specific reference to both local and national standards.

Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is ideally situated just a forty five minute drive from Manchester. The Trust provides services to the 440,000 residents of Blackpool, Fylde & Wyre and North Lancashire, as well as specialist tertiary care for Cardiac and Haematology patients.

descriptionHtml:

Are you a Consultant Psychiatrist looking for an exciting opportunity to provide clinical leadership and shape the future of mental health services?

Avon and Wiltshire Mental Health Partnership NHS Trust (AWP) is committed to delivering high-quality, compassionate care and driving innovation across our services. We are seeking a motivated Consultant Psychiatrist to join our South Gloucestershire locality, working across two key services: the Inpatient Open Rehabilitation Unit at 37 Whittucks Road, Hanham, and the Primary Care Liaison Service (PCLS) at Kingswood Civic Centre.

This varied role offers the opportunity to influence care across inpatient and community settings. Within the Rehabilitation Unit, you will provide clinical and medical leadership, supporting the development of rehabilitation services across South Gloucestershire and BNSSG.

In the PCLS, you will strengthen an established multidisciplinary team, helping to meet growing demand, expand clinical capacity, and improve access to specialist mental health support within primary care.

Join a forward-thinking Trust where your expertise, leadership and ideas will help shape services and improve outcomes for the communities we serve.

This is an exciting opportunity to work across two established services within South Gloucestershire: the Primary Care Liaison Service (PCLS) and the Inpatient Open Rehabilitation Unit.

Within PCLS, you will provide specialist psychiatric assessment and treatment for service users in the community, undertaking both initial medical assessments and follow-up reviews. You will be an active member of the multidisciplinary team, attending daily triage and clinical discussion meetings, providing medical expertise to support patient care, and offering advice and guidance to GPs and other healthcare professionals.

Within the Open Rehabilitation Unit, you will provide consultant leadership and comprehensive psychiatric care to inpatients, including direct and indirect clinical care, supervision of junior medical staff, consultation with colleagues, and multidisciplinary working. You will also lead the review of out-of-area placements for BSW service users, working collaboratively with community teams, social care, and partner agencies to support repatriation to local services through personalised rehabilitation pathways and recovery-focused care plans.

The post offers opportunities to contribute to clinical leadership, service development, teaching, supervision, and quality improvement across both inpatient and community settings.

We are AWP (Avon and Wiltshire Mental Health Partnership NHS Trust) a diverse organisation with over 5,000 dedicated staff providing inpatient and community-based mental health care. We provide services from a range of locations to approximately 1.8 million people living in Bath and North East Somerset (B&NES), Bristol, North Somerset, South Gloucestershire, Swindon, across the county of Wiltshire.

Our outstanding people promote mental health and wellbeing. The expertise and resources within AWP are dedicated to a person-centred approach for those who use our services and for all employees. We recognise that happy and fulfilled employees give better care.

At AWP we actively encourage applicants from all backgrounds; we are particularly keen to encourage applications from people from Black, Asian and minority ethnic backgrounds, those with disabilities and from the LGBTQ+ community. We want people to bring their unique blend of experiences, backgrounds, perspectives and knowledge to AWP, as diversity makes us stronger.

title: Consultant Radionuclide Radiologist/Nuclear Medicine Physician
descriptionHtml:
We are recognised as one of the leading NHS Foundation Trusts in the UK, supporting around 2.8 million patient appointments every year. The Trust is a regional centre for cancer, trauma, burns & plastics and has the largest solid organ transplantation programme in Europe. Due to growth in services, particularly PET-CT, applications are invited for a permanent Consultant Radionuclide Radiologist with special interest in PET-CT/Nuclear Medicine. QEHB hosts the regional PET Centre with one of the busiest PET-CT scanners in the country with a new two-scanner PET Centre on the horizon. The Nuclear Medicine Department also performs a wide range of diagnostic imaging, in-patient and out-patient therapies and non-imaging tests, and supports numerous clinical trials. We have 3 SPECT-CT systems in the department including the first 64-slice Veriton in the UK. We have an on-site radiopharmacy and produce Gallium-68 (PSMA/Dota-peptide). The QEHB nuclear medicine department has a staff of 66 including 7 Radionuclide Radiologists and Nuclear Cardiologists. Duties will include general nuclear medicine and PET-CT reporting and participation in MDMs. Experience in radionuclide therapies will be welcomed but is not essential. There will be a requirement for a single acute inpatient CT reporting session in the job plan. The post is otherwise NM/ PET CT only and, as such, there will be no involvement in the diagnostic radiology on-call and no scope for additional subspeciality work

Duties will include reporting of general nuclear medicine and PET-CT studies as well as participation in specialist MDT meetings on behalf of the service. The postholder must be familiar with supporting a comprehensive Nuclear Medicine service including a wide range of both imaging and non-imaging studies, PET imaging including F-18 and Ga-68 tracers) and a large Radiopharmacy service. The post holder will act as an IR(ME)R practitioner (ARSAC practitioner) with a license covering the services provided in the Trust. Key skills with experience in justifying studies, answering clinical queries, troubleshooting, protocol development, study optimisation, radiation protection matters, audit and clinical governance are expected

The post-holder will be required to participate in out-of- hours Nuclear Medicine advice and guidance (ARSAC) (approx. 1 in 8). The scope of ARSAC cover is expected to expand with the upcoming new national PET contract, which may include planned out-of-hours PET CT reporting

Good communication skills with a wide range of key clinical staff is required. The post holder is expected to contribute and support to the teaching and training of a wide range of staff groups in the department

Experience in radionuclide therapies is welcomed but is not essential

title: Consultant Radiologist - Interventional
descriptionHtml:
An opportunity to join an established interventional radiology service and help shape its future development

The highly regarded, forward-thinking Radiology Department at Hampshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is seeking an enthusiastic and motivated substantive Consultant Interventional Radiologist to join our friendly and ambitious team. This permanent appointment offers the opportunity to contribute to an established interventional radiology service, work across a broad range of procedures and help shape the future direction of the service across Hampshire Hospitals and the wider regional network.

This is an exciting time to join Hampshire Hospitals. We have invested in our interventional radiology service, with refurbishment and modernisation of our angiography suites to provide a modern clinical environment. We are looking for a colleague with a strong interest in vascular and general interventional radiology who would also welcome the opportunity to contribute to the ongoing development of our interventional oncology service.

The successful candidate will work across Basingstoke and North Hampshire Hospital and the Royal Hampshire County Hospital in Winchester, delivering a broad range of vascular and non-vascular interventional radiology procedures. Our established workload includes peripheral vascular intervention, embolisation, venous intervention, nephrostomy and biliary intervention, image-guided drainage and biopsy, vascular access and other minimally invasive treatments.

We are particularly interested in recruiting a colleague with a strong vascular interest and a broad-based general interventional radiology practice who is keen to develop their clinical interests within a supportive and collaborative team.

Alongside our established interventional workload, our interventional oncology service continues to develop, creating opportunities for the successful candidate to become involved in and contribute to the growth of minimally invasive oncological treatments, including tumour ablation and other image-guided therapies. We would welcome someone enthusiastic about developing their experience and expertise in this area and helping shape the future direction of the service.

Across HHFT we currently have 2 IR/Fluoro rooms and 1 Interventional room, 2 clinical rooms for ultrasound guided procedures, and day case recovery faculties on each site, 5 static CT scanners and 3 static MRI scanners (details below). This includes a private imaging facility on the Basingstoke site (Candover Clinic) which is part of the NHS trust and offers general X-ray, ultrasound, CT and MRI. Insignia PACS, CRIS and Talking point Voice Recognition are integrated across HHFT (PACS system undergoing replacement currently). Home-reporting workstations are provided for all Consultant Radiologists to facilitate the on-call service, flexible reporting and additional voluntary reporting ('insourcing').

The diagnostic on-call runs from 1700 - 2000 weekdays and 0900 - 2000 at the weekend, a separate rota for each site. An out of hours IR service is provided via a regional network with Frimley Health Foundation Trust.

The trust has recently committed to a multi-million pound programme of investment to refresh diagnostic imaging equipment over the next 10 years. The department has already benefited from a completely new fleet of Ultrasound machines, new X-ray rooms, and a new CT scanner. Two new MRI scanners are to be installed at the end of 2023.
